title: Thyroid hormones and lipid profiles in ART-treated versus ART-naïve adults living with HIV: a cross-sectional study in Western Kenya
abstractText: Abstract Background ART has reduced HIV mortality, but dyslipidaemia and thyroid dysfunction are increasingly observed; effects in Kisumu County remain unclear. Methodology Serum lipids (TC, TG, HDL, LDL) and thyroid hormones (TSH, T4, T3) were assessed in 84 ART-treated and 20 ART-naïve subjects using colorimetric and immunofluorescence methods. Mann–Whitney U and Spearman’s correlation tests were used. Results ART-treated subjects had higher TSH [1.72 (1.71) vs 0.87 (1.07) nmo/L, P = 0.001]. T4, HDL, TC, TG, and LDL did not differ significantly. T4 positively correlated with LDL ( P = 0.014). Conclusion ART is linked to elevated TSH; routine lipid and thyroid monitoring is advised.

title: EXPLORING LEARNING GAPS AND SUPPORT NEEDS IN DIFFERENTIATION AND INTEGRATION TOPIC
abstractText: The purpose of this research was to explore any learning difficulties faced by students enrolled in Differentiation and Integration under the course DBM20173 of Engineering Mathematics 2. The aim was to pinpoint possible reasons that affected students’ comprehension and utilization of concepts of calculus, especially for questions related to interpretation, selection of methods, visualization, and problem-solving. This was accomplished using a combination of methods, namely, pre-test results, error identification, survey from students, interview or focus group discussion and observation by lecturer. The results revealed that students experienced difficulty only with the unfamiliar and application-based questions rather than direct procedural ones. According to the pre-test results, volume of bounded regions represented the highest number of difficulties among the participants with 25 out of 30 participants (83.3%), while trigonometric, exponential and reciprocal integration involved 24 students (80.0%) and area under a curve involved 23 students (76.7%). As many as 248 errors occurred during the process; formula error was found to be the most common type of errors occurring in 58 cases (23.4%), while visualisation error occurred in 43 cases (17.3%), followed by method-selection error with 42 occurrences (16.9%). The questionnaire results revealed that the level of readiness to engage in digital and immersive learning assistance was very high, as the mean score equaled 4.39, while need for visualisation and application-based assistance was also very high (mean score 4.34).

title: Penurunan Kadar BOD pada Limbah Cair Tapioka melalui Metode Filtrasi Dilanjutkan dengan Biofiltrasi
abstractText: Limbah cair dari industri tapioka memiliki beban pencemar organik yang tinggi, ditandai dengan nilai Biochemical Oxygen Demand (BOD) yang melebihi ambang batas baku mutu lingkungan. Penelitian ini bertujuan untuk mengevaluasi efektivitas sistem pengolahan kombinasi fisik dan biologis, yaitu filtrasi menggunakan pasir silika dan biofiltrasi menggunakan media plastik, dalam menurunkan kadar BOD limbah cair tapioka. Metode penelitian dilakukan secara eksperimental dengan sistem batch, menerapkan variasi waktu kontak filtrasi selama 5, 10, dan 15 menit, serta waktu tinggal biofiltrasi selama 7, 14, dan 21 hari. Hasil analisis menunjukkan bahwa BOD awal limbah sebesar 425 mg/L mengalami penurunan melalui tahapan pengolahan. Pada tahap filtrasi dengan pasir silika, penurunan optimal terjadi pada waktu kontak 15 menit menjadi 419 mg/L dengan efektivitas 1,41%, yang berfungsi sebagai tahap prapengolahan untuk menyisihkan padatan. Pengolahan dilanjutkan dengan biofiltrasi media plastik, yang terbukti sangat signifikan menurunkan kadar BOD hingga mencapai 15 mg/L pada hari ke-21 dengan efektivitas penurunan sebesar 96,42%. Hasil akhir pengolahan ini telah memenuhi standar baku mutu Peraturan Menteri Lingkungan Hidup RI Nomor 5 Tahun 2014, yaitu di bawah 150 mg/L. Disimpulkan bahwa integrasi metode filtrasi dan biofiltrasi merupakan solusi yang efisien dan efektif untuk mendegradasi polutan organik pada limbah cair tapioka.

title: Perancangan Game Edukasi Kebersihan Lingkungan 2D Side-Scrolling Berbasis Godot Engine dengan Metode MDLC
abstractText: Permasalahan sampah di Indonesia masih menjadi isu lingkungan yang serius, salah satunya karena rendahnya kebiasaan masyarakat memilah sampah dari sumbernya, sedangkan penyampaian materi edukasi yang kurang bervariasi berpotensi menurunkan minat belajar. Penelitian ini bertujuan merancang dan mengembangkan game edukasi kebersihan lingkungan 2D side-scrolling berbasis Godot Engine serta mengetahui tingkat kelayakannya sebagai media edukasi pengenalan dan pemilahan sampah. Pengembangan menggunakan metode Multimedia Development Life Cycle (MDLC) yang meliputi tahap concept, design, material collecting, assembly, testing, dan distribution. Game diimplementasikan menggunakan Godot Engine 4 dengan bahasa GDScript dan diuji secara fungsional dengan metode white box dan black box. Uji kelayakan dilakukan melalui kuesioner berisi 10 pernyataan berskala Likert lima poin kepada 69 responden yang dipilih dengan teknik accidental sampling, kemudian dianalisis menggunakan metode persentase. Hasil penelitian berupa game berjudul “Tony dan Dunia yang Tercampur” yang terdiri atas tiga level dengan tingkat kesulitan bertahap. Setiap level memuat fase runner untuk mengumpulkan sampah dan menghindari rintangan, serta fase pemilahan sampah organik, anorganik, dan Bahan Berbahaya dan Beracun (B3) sesuai warna tempat sampah. Pengujian white box pada lima modul dan black box pada lima skenario menunjukkan seluruh fungsi berjalan sesuai rancangan. Uji kelayakan menghasilkan total skor 3.185 dari skor ideal 3.450 atau sebesar 92,32% dengan kategori sangat layak, dengan persentase tertinggi pada aspek pemahaman klasifikasi sampah setelah bermain (93,62%).

title: Pemberdayaan Masyarakat Berbasis Rukun Tetangga (RT) dalam Pencegahan Tindak Pidana Kekerasan Seksual di Kawasan Mampang, Jakarta Selatan
abstractText: Kekerasan seksual masih menjadi persoalan sosial dan hukum yang serius, sementara partisipasi masyarakat dalam pencegahannya di tingkat lingkungan permukiman belum optimal. Kegiatan pengabdian kepada masyarakat ini bertujuan meningkatkan pengetahuan, kesadaran hukum, dan partisipasi warga berbasis Rukun Tetangga (RT) dalam pencegahan tindak pidana kekerasan seksual di kawasan Mampang, Jakarta Selatan. Kegiatan menggunakan metode deskriptif kualitatif dengan pendekatan partisipatif dan edukatif yang dilaksanakan dalam empat tahap, yaitu persiapan, sosialisasi dan edukasi hukum berdasarkan Undang-Undang Nomor 12 Tahun 2022 tentang Tindak Pidana Kekerasan Seksual, diskusi interaktif, serta evaluasi. Sasaran kegiatan meliputi pengurus RT, tokoh masyarakat, pemuda, orang tua, dan warga. Data dikumpulkan melalui observasi, dokumentasi, diskusi, dan kuesioner, kemudian dianalisis secara deskriptif. Hasil kegiatan menunjukkan bahwa peserta mengikuti seluruh sesi dengan antusias, aktif bertanya dan berdiskusi, serta mampu memberikan tanggapan yang relevan terhadap materi. Peserta memperoleh pemahaman mengenai bentuk dan dampak kekerasan seksual, hak-hak korban, mekanisme pelaporan dan pendampingan, serta pentingnya mencegah stigma dan tindakan menyalahkan korban (victim blaming). Kegiatan ini juga menegaskan kedudukan RT sebagai basis pengorganisasian sosial dalam penyebarluasan edukasi hukum, pemberian dukungan awal kepada korban, dan penghubungan korban dengan lembaga layanan yang berwenang. Pemberdayaan berbasis RT berpotensi menjadi strategi pencegahan kekerasan seksual yang berkelanjutan apabila didukung oleh pemerintah setempat dan lembaga perlindungan.

title: ADAPTATION OF THE TNI AD'S CAVALRY EDUCATION AND TRAINING SYSTEM TO THE CHARACTER OF MODERN WARFARE
abstractText: The changing character of modern warfare has expanded the competencies required of Indonesian Army Cavalry personnel, particularly in responding to UAS and counter-UAS threats, electronic warfare, networked command and control, and combined-arms and multidomain operations. This study aims to analyze the adaptation of the Indonesian Army Cavalry education and training system, identify remaining gaps, and formulate relevant directions for improvement. It employs a qualitative approach with a descriptive-analytical case study design. Pusdikkav serves as the primary locus, while Pussenkav TNI AD and Yonkav 1 Kostrad provide complementary perspectives on branch development, education, and unit requirements. Data are collected through semi-structured interviews, limited observation, documentation, and literature review, and are analyzed thematically with SWOT used as a strategic analytical tool. The findings indicate that adaptation has begun through the use of battlefield management systems, integrated training, and the introduction of unmanned technologies, yet institutionalization across curricula, training methods, instructor competence, learning facilities, and interoperability remains uneven. The study highlights the need to move toward system-oriented training, strengthen instructor capacity, integrate learning technologies, expand interoperability training, and establish a continuous unit-feedback mechanism to maintain the relevance of Cavalry education amid changing operational demands.

title: LITERASI SAINS, KETERAMPILAN PROSES SAINS, DAN HASIL BELAJAR BERBASIS HOTS
abstractText: Abstrak Kemampuan berpikir tingkat tinggi (higher order thinking skills/HOTS) merupakan kompetensi penting bagi calon guru, termasuk dalam pembelajaran IPA di Program Studi Pendidikan Guru Madrasah Ibtidaiyah (PGMI). Literasi sains dan keterampilan proses sains diduga berkaitan dengan pencapaian HOTS. Penelitian ini bertujuan menganalisis hubungan literasi sains dan keterampilan proses sains dengan hasil belajar kognitif berbasis HOTS mahasiswa PGMI. Penelitian kuantitatif dengan desain korelasional ini melibatkan 50 mahasiswa PGMI semester IV Universitas Islam Negeri Sulthan Thaha Saifuddin Jambi yang dipilih melalui proportional random sampling, dan dilaksanakan pada Juli 2025, semester genap 2024/2025. Data dikumpulkan dengan tes literasi sains, tes keterampilan proses sains, dan tes hasil belajar kognitif HOTS, kemudian dianalisis menggunakan regresi linear sederhana dan berganda setelah dilakukan uji asumsi klasik yang meliputi uji normalitas, linearitas, multikolinearitas, dan heteroskedastisitas. Hasil menunjukkan bahwa literasi sains dan keterampilan proses sains, baik secara parsial maupun simultan, berhubungan positif dan signifikan dengan HOTS. Model regresi berganda yang memuat kedua variabel menjelaskan 95,3% variasi HOTS (R = 0,976; R² = 0,953; p < 0,05. Karena kedua prediktor saling berkorelasi, kontribusi masing-masing variabel tidak dapat dijumlahkan. Mengingat desain korelasional, temuan ini menunjukkan keterkaitan statistik dan belum dapat dimaknai sebagai hubungan sebab-akibat. Temuan ini menegaskan pentingnya penguatan literasi sains dan keterampilan proses sains secara terpadu dalam pembelajaran IPA di Program Studi PGMI sebagai upaya mendukung pengembangan kemampuan berpikir tingkat tinggi mahasiswa calon guru MI. Kata Kunci: Literasi Sains; Keterampilan Proses Sains; Berpikir Tingkat Tinggi; PGMI; Regresi Abstract Higher order thinking skills (HOTS) are essential competencies for prospective teachers, particularly in science learning within the Islamic Primary School Teacher Education (PGMI) Study Program. Scientific literacy and science process skills are considered to be associated with the achievement of HOTS. This study aims to analyze the relationship between scientific literacy, science process skills, and HOTS-based cognitive learning outcomes among PGMI students. This quantitative study employed a correlational design involving 50 fourth-semester students of the State Islamic University of Sulthan Thaha Saifuddin Jambi, selected through proportional random sampling. The study was conducted in July 2025 during the second semester of the 2024/2025 academic year. Data were collected using scientific literacy tests, science process skills tests, and HOTS-based cognitive achievement tests. The data were analyzed using simple and multiple linear regression after conducting classical assumption tests, including normality, linearity, multicollinearity, and heteroscedasticity tests. The results indicate that scientific literacy and science process skills are positively and significantly associated with HOTS, both individually and jointly. The multiple regression model incorporating both variables explains 95.3% of the variance in HOTS (R = 0.976; R² = 0.953; p < 0.05). Since the two predictors are correlated, their individual contributions cannot simply be added together. Given the correlational design, these findings indicate statistical associations and cannot be interpreted as evidence of causal relationships. These findings underscore the importance of strengthening scientific literacy and science process skills in an integrated manner in science learning within the PGMI Study Program to support the development of higher order thinking skills among prospective Islamic primary school teachers. title: Leadership and Teamwork: Peran Kepemimpinan Empatik dalam Membangun Kerja Sama Tim dan Meningkatkan Efektivitas Organisasi
abstractText: Kepemimpinan dan kerja sama tim merupakan dua aspek penting dalam menentukan keberhasilan organisasi. Dalam lingkungan kerja yang semakin kompleks, seorang pemimpin tidak hanya dituntut memiliki kemampuan mengarahkan dan mengendalikan pekerjaan, tetapi juga memahami kondisi emosional, kebutuhan, serta kesulitan yang dialami anggota tim. Penelitian ini bertujuan menganalisis peran kepemimpinan empatik dalam membangun kerja sama tim dan mendukung efektivitas organisasi. Penelitian menggunakan pendekatan kualitatif deskriptif melalui metode studi pustaka (literature review), dengan mengkaji empat artikel utama dan sejumlah literatur pendukung yang relevan. Hasil sintesis literatur menunjukkan bahwa kepemimpinan empatik berpotensi memperkuat komunikasi terbuka, kepercayaan interpersonal, keamanan psikologis, motivasi, dan keterlibatan anggota tim. Faktor-faktor tersebut menjadi landasan bagi terbentuknya kolaborasi yang lebih efektif. Kepemimpinan empatik juga menempatkan kesejahteraan anggota sebagai bagian penting dari keberlanjutan organisasi. Penelitian ini menyimpulkan bahwa empati perlu dipandang sebagai kompetensi strategis kepemimpinan, bukan sekadar bentuk kepedulian pribadi. Penerapannya perlu diimbangi dengan pembagian tanggung jawab, keadilan, komunikasi yang jelas, serta evaluasi kinerja yang objektif.

title: Efektivitas Pengelolaan Administrasi Kepesertaan PNS dan PPPK Aktif dalam Mendukung Efisiensi Pelayanan Hak Pensiun pada PT Taspen (Persero) Kantor Cabang Surabaya
abstractText: Pengelolaan administrasi kepesertaan menjadi salah satu unsur penting dalam menunjang kelancaran pelayanan hak peserta di PT TASPEN (Persero). Ketepatan dan kelengkapan data kepesertaan diperlukan untuk mendukung proses administrasi serta memudahkan pencarian informasi peserta ketika memasuki masa pensiun. Penelitian ini bertujuan untuk mengetahui peran pengelolaan administrasi kepesertaan PNS dan PPPK aktif dalam mendukung efisiensi pelayanan hak pensiun pada PT TASPEN (Persero) Kantor Cabang Surabaya. Penelitian ini menggunakan pendekatan kualitatif deskriptif dengan pelaksanaan kegiatan pada 31 Agustus sampai 30 Oktober 2026. Data penelitian diperoleh melalui observasi selama kegiatan magang dan wawancara dengan lima pegawai pada bagian Kepesertaan dan Pelayanan. Analisis data dilakukan melalui tahapan pengumpulan data, reduksi data, penyajian data, dan penarikan kesimpulan. Hasil penelitian menunjukkan bahwa pengelolaan administrasi kepesertaan berperan dalam menjaga ketepatan dan kelengkapan informasi peserta, menunjang pengolahan data gaji dan iuran, serta memudahkan pencarian dokumen administrasi. Pengelolaan tersebut turut mendukung proses pelayanan hak pensiun karena data kepesertaan yang tersusun dengan baik dapat mempermudah pelaksanaan administrasi pada tahap selanjutnya. Dengan demikian, ketelitian dalam pemutakhiran data dan pemenuhan kelengkapan dokumen menjadi hal yang perlu diperhatikan guna menunjang kelancaran pelayanan kepada peserta.

title: Analisis Prosedur Verifikasi dan Rekonsiliasi Transaksi Keuangan pada Program Jaminan Kecelakaan Kerja pada PT Taspen (Persero) Kantor Cabang Surabaya
abstractText: Penelitian ini bertujuan untuk mengetahui penerapan verifikasi dan rekonsiliasi data transaksi keuangan Program Jaminan Kecelakaan Kerja (JKK) pada PT TASPEN (Persero) Kantor Cabang Surabaya. Penelitian dilaksanakan di Jalan Diponegoro No. 193, Wonokromo, Surabaya, pada 31 Agustus sampai dengan 30 September 2026. Penelitian menggunakan pendekatan kualitatif deskriptif dengan teknik pengumpulan data berupa observasi partisipatif dan studi dokumen. Sumber data diperoleh dari catatan pengamatan penulis selama kegiatan Praktik Pengalaman Lapangan (PPL), dokumen administrasi pengajuan tagihan biaya perawatan JKK, serta informasi dari petugas melalui diskusi informal. Analisis data dilakukan melalui reduksi data, penyajian data, dan penarikan kesimpulan. Hasil penelitian menunjukkan bahwa verifikasi dilakukan dengan memeriksa identitas peserta, informasi kecelakaan kerja, status penjaminan, kelengkapan dokumen, dan kesesuaian rincian tagihan rumah sakit. Sementara itu, rekonsiliasi dilakukan melalui pencocokan informasi antardokumen dan bukti transaksi untuk mengetahui kemungkinan perbedaan data maupun nominal. Kendala yang perlu diperhatikan dalam proses tersebut meliputi ketidaklengkapan dokumen dan ketidaksesuaian informasi. Tindak lanjut dilakukan melalui pemeriksaan ulang dokumen sumber, konfirmasi kepada pihak terkait, serta pencatatan hasil klarifikasi. Penelitian ini diharapkan dapat menjadi bahan evaluasi bagi perusahaan dalam memperkuat ketelitian pemeriksaan dan ketertiban administrasi keuangan Program JKK.

title: Manajemen Pelayanan Konsumen pada Layanan Transportasi Publik Trans Jawa Timur Koridor Malang
abstractText: The Trans East Java Corridor Malang public transportation plays a vital role in mobility and tourism but still faces constraints like schedule inconsistencies, digital information accuracy, and responsiveness. This study aims to analyze the effect of customer service management on customer satisfaction. This quantitative research uses a descriptive-analytical method with an accidental sampling technique involving 100 respondents. Data were collected via questionnaires, observation, and documentation, then analyzed using validity, reliability, simple linear regression, t-test, and coefficient of determination. The results show that customer service management has a positive and significant effect on customer satisfaction. Regression analysis yielded a constant of 1.404 and a regression coefficient of 0.233. Hypothesis testing proved the t-count (17.866) is greater than the t-table (1.66055) with a significance of 0.000 < 0.05. The correlation coefficient (R) of 0.875 indicates a very strong relationship, with a determination coefficient (R Square) of 0.765, meaning customer service management contributes 76.5% to customer satisfaction variance, while 23.5% is explained by other factors. Tangible and assurance aspects received the highest passenger assessments. Conclusively, improving service quality, operational punctuality, and digital information accuracy is highly essential to achieve sustainable and long-term customer satisfaction.

title: Komunikasi Kelompok dalam Membangun Solidaritas Mahasiswa Perantauan pada Paguyuban Keluarga Mahasiswa Tebing Tinggi Bersatu (KATIBER) di Lhokseumawe-aceh Utara
abstractText: Komunikasi kelompok memiliki peran penting dalam membangun hubungan sosial dan solidaritas mahasiswa perantauan yang tergabung dalam organisasi daerah. Penelitian ini bertujuan untuk mendeskripsikan komunikasi kelompok dalam membangun solidaritas mahasiswa perantauan pada Paguyuban Keluarga Mahasiswa Tebing Tinggi Bersatu (KATIBER) di Lhokseumawe dan Aceh Utara serta mengidentifikasi hambatan komunikasi yang terjadi. Penelitian ini menggunakan pendekatan kualitatif dengan jenis deskriptif. Informan dipilih melalui teknik purposive sampling yang melibatkan enam orang, yaitu ketua, sekretaris, ketua humas, anggota Universitas Malikussaleh, demisioner, dan anggota Politeknik. Data dikumpulkan melalui observasi nonpartisipan, wawancara semi-terstruktur, dan dokumentasi, kemudian dianalisis melalui reduksi data, penyajian data, serta penarikan kesimpulan dan verifikasi. Hasil penelitian menunjukkan bahwa komunikasi kelompok KATIBER berlangsung melalui interaksi tatap muka dan grup WhatsApp dengan melibatkan enam unsur Model Komunikasi Transaksional Dean Barnlund. Komunikasi tersebut mendukung terbentuknya solidaritas melalui kebersamaan, kepercayaan, kepedulian, dan kerja sama antaranggota. Hambatan komunikasi meliputi perbedaan jadwal perkuliahan, kesibukan anggota, keterlambatan membaca pesan, dan terbatasnya respons dalam grup WhatsApp. Komunikasi dua arah dan koordinasi berkelanjutan diperlukan untuk meningkatkan partisipasi anggota serta menjaga solidaritas organisasi.

title: Kepemimpinan Transformasional, Kepuasan Kerja, dan Kinerja Karyawan: Peran Mediasi Komitmen Organisasi pada Suku Dinas Tenaga Kerja, Transmigrasi, dan Energi Kota Jakarta Utara
abstractText: Kinerja Karyawan pada instansi pelayanan publik berkaitan dengan kepemimpinan atasan, kepuasan kerja, dan komitmen pegawai terhadap organisasi. Penelitian ini bertujuan menguji pengaruh kepemimpinan transformasional dan kepuasan kerja terhadap Kinerja Karyawan serta peran komitmen organisasi sebagai variabel mediasi pada Suku Dinas Tenaga Kerja, Transmigrasi, dan Energi Kota Administrasi Jakarta Utara. Penelitian menggunakan pendekatan kuantitatif melalui survei kuesioner dengan skala Likert 1–4 terhadap seluruh pegawai pada lima unit kerja (sensus; N = 100), setelah pretest terhadap 34 pegawai di luar sampel utama. Data dianalisis menggunakan Partial Least Squares Structural Equation Modeling (PLS-SEM) dengan SmartPLS 4. Hasil evaluasi model pengukuran menunjukkan bahwa seluruh konstruk memenuhi kriteria validitas dan reliabilitas, dengan AVE sebesar 0,600–0,783 dan composite reliability sebesar 0,899–0,940. Hasil pengujian menunjukkan bahwa kepemimpinan transformasional (β = 0,468) dan kepuasan kerja (β = 0,394) berpengaruh positif dan signifikan terhadap Kinerja Karyawan. Kepuasan kerja juga berpengaruh positif terhadap komitmen organisasi (β = 0,607), sedangkan kepemimpinan transformasional tidak berpengaruh signifikan terhadap komitmen organisasi (β = −0,059). Komitmen organisasi berpengaruh positif dan signifikan terhadap Kinerja Karyawan (β = 0,487) serta memediasi pengaruh kepuasan kerja terhadap Kinerja Karyawan (β = 0,174), tetapi tidak memediasi pengaruh kepemimpinan transformasional terhadap Kinerja Karyawan. Dengan demikian, lima hipotesis didukung (H1, H2, H4, H5, dan H7), sedangkan H3 dan H6 tidak didukung. Temuan ini menunjukkan pentingnya kepemimpinan transformasional, kepuasan kerja, dan komitmen organisasi dalam mendukung kinerja pegawai pada instansi yang diteliti.

title: Model AISAS dalam Proses Pembentukan Loyalitas Pelanggan pada Akun @Warunghasturi
abstractText: Perkembangan media sosial mendorong pelaku usaha kuliner memanfaatkan komunikasi pemasaran digital untuk menarik perhatian konsumen dan mempertahankan loyalitas pelanggan. Penelitian ini bertujuan menganalisis komunikasi pemasaran digital melalui akun Instagram @warunghasturi berdasarkan model Attention, Interest, Search, Action, dan Share (AISAS) serta mengidentifikasi faktor-faktor pendukung pelaksanaannya dalam meningkatkan loyalitas pelanggan. Penelitian ini menggunakan pendekatan kualitatif dengan pengumpulan data melalui observasi, wawancara terstruktur, dan dokumentasi. Informan terdiri atas enam orang yang meliputi pemilik usaha, admin Instagram, pekerja, pengikut Instagram, dan konsumen. Data dianalisis menggunakan model interaktif Miles dan Huberman melalui reduksi data, penyajian data, serta penarikan kesimpulan. Hasil penelitian menunjukkan bahwa Warung Hasturi telah menerapkan kelima tahapan AISAS melalui konten visual, informasi produk, interaksi dengan pengikut, promosi, dan unggahan pengalaman pelanggan. Faktor pendukungnya meliputi konsistensi pengelolaan konten, kreativitas dan keragaman unggahan, interaksi dua arah, serta penyampaian informasi dan promosi produk. Loyalitas pelanggan terlihat dari pembelian ulang, kunjungan kembali, dan rekomendasi kepada orang lain. Penelitian ini menyimpulkan bahwa komunikasi pemasaran digital melalui Instagram dapat mendukung loyalitas pelanggan apabila diimbangi dengan kualitas produk, pelayanan, kenyamanan outlet, dan kesiapan operasional usaha.

title: Rinitis Alergi, Gangguan Sinonasal, dan Keberhasilan Miringoplasti: Tinjauan Naratif
abstractText: Fungsi tuba Eustachius dianggap berperan dalam keberhasilan penutupan membran timpani setelah miringoplasti, dan inflamasi atau obstruksi sinonasal secara teoretis dapat mengganggu fungsi tersebut. Tinjauan naratif ini merangkum bukti klinis mengenai hubungan rinitis alergi, rinitis nonalergi, rinosinusitis kronis, deviasi septum nasi, dan operasi hidung bersamaan dengan keberhasilan graft setelah miringoplasti atau timpanoplasti tipe I. Delapan studi klinis komparatif yang terbit pada 2015–2024 dibahas. Rinitis alergi tidak berhubungan bermakna dengan kegagalan graft pada tiga studi, meskipun studi terbesar menunjukkan keberhasilan yang lebih rendah secara numerik (80,8% vs 89,5%). Satu studi prospektif menemukan kegagalan graft hanya pada rinitis nonalergi (16,7%), sedangkan riwayat rinosinusitis kronis menjadi satu-satunya prediktor kegagalan anatomis pada satu seri miringoplasti kartilago (OR 4,29). Deviasi septum dan fungsi jalan napas hidung yang diukur secara objektif tidak berhubungan dengan luaran graft pada empat studi. Pada operasi hidung bersamaan, keberhasilan jangka pendek tinggi, tetapi satu studi melaporkan keberhasilan yang lebih rendah pada bulan ke-24 pada kelompok septoplasti. Bukti yang tersedia terbatas, sebagian besar retrospektif, dan heterogen dalam definisi paparan. Rinitis alergi dan deviasi septum tampaknya bukan kontraindikasi miringoplasti, sedangkan penyakit sinonasal inflamatorik sebaiknya dikendalikan sebelum operasi. Diperlukan studi kohort prospektif dengan penilaian sinonasal terstandar dan pemantauan minimal 12 bulan.

title: Tuned Fitness Landscapes for Benchmarking Model-Guided Protein Design
abstractText: Abstract Machine learning-guided directed evolution (MLDE) is an emerging paradigm of protein design where ML models trained on experimental data are used to guide exploration of a protein fitness landscape. Building an MLDE pipeline involves many design choices across the design-build-test-learn loop ranging from data collection strategies to modeling. The cost of collecting experimental data makes benchmarking every component of these pipelines prohibitively difficult, necessitating the development of synthetic landscapes. In this work, we develop a framework called SLIP (“Synthetic Landscape Inference for Proteins”) for constructing synthetic landscapes with tunable difficulty based on Potts models. This framework can be extended to any protein family for which there is a sequence alignment. We show that our tuning framework provides landscapes sufficiently challenging to benchmark MLDE pipelines. SLIP is open-source and is available at https://github.com/google-research/slip.

title: Enhancer-driven gene regulatory network of human forebrain development provides insights into autism
abstractText: Cell differentiation is orchestrated by transcription factors binding to enhancers, shaping gene regulatory networks that drive neuronal lineage specification. Deciphering these enhancer-driven networks in human forebrain development is essential for understanding the genetic basis of neurodevelopmental disorders. Through integrative epigenomic and transcriptomic analyses of human forebrain organoids derived from 10 male individuals with autism spectrum disorder and their neurotypical fathers, we construct a comprehensive enhancer-driven gene regulatory network of early neurodevelopment. This network reveals hierarchical regulatory layers upstream of neuronal cell fate genes, experimentally validated via CRISPR interference and loss-of-function analyses. A subnetwork links autism-associated transcriptomic alterations to opposite activities of the transcription factors FOXG1, BHLHE22, EOMES, and NEUROD2, driving increased or decreased excitatory neuron specification in (respectively) macrocephalic or normocephalic individuals with autism. These findings support the association of autism with disruption of enhancer-driven regulatory networks altering neuronal cell fate decisions in the developing fetal brain. The authors construct a gene regulatory network showing the potential role of specific enhancer elements in driving lineage imbalance in autism, explaining why forebrain organoids from autism probands show heterogeneity in the generation of excitatory neurons.

title: On R-Matrix Formulation of qq-Characters
abstractText: Abstract We introduce an R -matrix formulation of qq -characters and corresponding Frenkel–Reshetikhin deformed W -algebras. The R -matrix featuring in the construction is of Ding–Iohara–Miki (DIM) algebra, while the type of the qq -character is determined by the network of Fock representations corresponding to a web of 5-branes geometrically engineering a quiver gauge theory.Our formulation gives a unified description of qq -characters of $$A_n$$ A n type and their elliptic uplifts.

Cerebra: A computationally efficient framework for accurate protein structure prediction
abstractText: Abstract Remarkable progress has been made in the field of protein structure prediction. Representative methods like AlphaFold and RoseTTAFold achieve prediction accuracy close to experimental structural determination, but at the cost of heavy computational consumption for model training. In this work, we propose a new framework, Cerebra, for improving the computational efficiency of protein structure prediction. In this network architecture, multiple sets of atomic coordinates are predicted parallelly and their mutual complementarity is leveraged to rapidly improve the quality of predicted structures through a new attention mechanism named path synthesis attention (PSA). Consequently, Cerebra markedly reduces the computational consumption, achieving evident acceleration on both model training and inference, in comparison to OpenFold, the academic version of AlphaFold2. When evaluated on the CAMEO 2025 dataset, the Cerebra model trained on a limited number of GPUs shows comparable performance to the published OpenFold model that has been thoroughly optimized using a plethora of computational resources. Moreover, ablation studies confirm that the PSA mechanism efficiently accelerates the network convergence, suggesting its potential in handling the many‐body effects of protein geometries in graph‐based models. Finally, the fast inference of Cerebra effectively assists hallucination‐based de novo protein backbone design, allowing the production of abundant backbone structures with sufficient designability and novelty.

title: Deep multimodal K-fold Model for emotion and sentiment analysis in figurative language
abstractText: Abstract The “Deep multimodal K-fold model” is an approach to machine learning that uses multiple modalities, such as text and audio, to analyze emotion and sentiment in Figurative Language. This model uses a K-fold cross-validation method to test how well it works and ensure it can be used in other situations. Using the CMU-MOSEI (Carnegie Mellon University Multimodal Opinion Sentiment and Emotion Intensity) database, we explore sentiment and emotion, considering various aspects like ironic, sarcastic, and subjective sentences in this study. We have four models in our deep learning analysis approach (audio emotion, text emotion, text sentiment, and audio sentiment). We suggested a single-tasking multimodal framework outperforming others to benefit from the interdependence of two related activities (sentiment and emotion). Our experiment was conducted using CNN and LSTM. Specific experimental findings show that LSTM performs better than CNN for the two emotion models, whereas CNN is slightly better for the two sentiment models. We achieved 99% accuracy in the k-Fold Deep Learning Text Emotion model and 88% in the k-Fold Deep Learning Audio Emotion model with the LSTM technique (85% and 85% with CNN). In text and audio sentiment analysis, we got 94% and 79% with CNN (93% and 78% with LSTM), respectively. All reported figures are accuracies on a single held-out test split rather than averages over the K folds. In conclusion, the Deep multimodal K-fold model is a promising way to analyze emotions and feelings in Figurative Language. Within the limits of the single-split evaluation on a 1,354-utterance subset reported here, it offers a reliable baseline for this task because it combines multiple modalities with K-fold cross-validation.

title: Finding the right balance: a framework analysis of staff and service user experiences of moving to remote drug and alcohol support during the COVID-19 pandemic
abstractText: Abstract Background Dependence on alcohol and other substances contributes significantly to poor health globally. Deaths associated with substance use have increased since the COVID-19 pandemic and providing effective support for recovery is critical. The pandemic required an unprecedented change to recovery services for substance use, from in-person care to mainly telephone and online support. The study described here forms part of a wider evaluation and was one of the first to explore the move to remote models of recovery services. Methods This was a multi-method qualitative study, employing in-depth interviews, focus groups, text-based asynchronous interviews, digital timelines and creative vignettes. Framework analysis was undertaken, with focus on service user out-of-pocket expenses as part of a health economic evaluation. A Public Involvement group, including people with experience of substance use, supported study design and analysis. Staff ( N = 36) and drug and alcohol service users ( N = 28) in an English city participated in one or more of the data collection methods. Findings were shared with staff and service users, and their input shaped the final analysis. Results Most participants wanted to retain remote services alongside in-person provision, post-pandemic. Remote delivery was not appropriate for everyone however, and not all aspects of service delivery work remotely. Findings are organized under two main themes. Within the first, Finding the Right Balance , factors contributing to an improved service experience for some are contrasted with reduced information on which staff can base judgements and other risks to service user wellbeing. Within the second, Resourcing Hybrid , some of the resource implications for providers, (e.g. hybrid optimised service hubs), and users (e.g. digital access) are drawn out. Conclusions Drug and alcohol services should include remote support options for some service users where that is likely to be safe and enhance their care. In-person and outreach or home-visiting will be more appropriate for some. Services may need to invest in training and resourcing for a hybrid offer to operate effectively. Service user preferences and their personal resources, health and wellbeing, and whether they are able to engage with the service as offered should be central to how their care is planned. Dichotomies uniform on subspaces and formulas for dichotomy spectra
abstractText: We introduce a notion of dichotomy which generalizes the classical concept of exponential dichotomy and the recent notion of Bohl dichotomy. A key attribute is the discussion of the sets of subspaces of the state space on which the dichotomy estimates are uniform. Two main results are a dichotomy spectral theorem based on our notion of dichotomy which is uniform on subspaces and a formula for the dichotomy spectral intervals which is new for the Bohl dichotomy spectrum as well as for the classical exponential dichotomy spectrum.

title: Fair and Online Itinerary Recommendation for Multiple Visitors in Crowded Destinations
abstractText: Coordinating tourist trips in congested destinations allows for higher user satisfaction and reduced waiting times. A new online problem is introduced to allow the recommendation of tourist-trip itineraries when only limited information is available on arriving tourists. We propose a recommender system for generating congestion-aware itineraries in real time for a large number of tourists. The goal of the algorithm is to suggest high quality itinerary recommendations which lead to a fair allocation of tourists to points of interest. We test this method using different underlying heuristics. Numerical experiments show that the proposed algorithm outperforms a First-Come-First-Served policy and performs reasonably close to offline methods. The online algorithm is able to solve realistically sized problem instances with competitive running times. We find that for realistically sized instances, methods based on an iterated local search heuristic result in flatter distributions of score over users than those based on a greedy randomized adaptive search procedure.

title: Genotoxic stress responses in wild-type and Nijmegen Breakage Syndrome hiPSC and NPC models of early development
abstractText: Abstract Benzo[a]pyrene diol epoxide (BPDE), a metabolite of Benzo[a]pyrene, is a byproduct of incomplete combustion of organic matter. The accumulation of BPDE-DNA bulky adducts can lead to mutations caused by DNA base-pair substitutions. Although the effects of BPDE on somatic cells have been described, its harmful effects on early human development have not been studied. Here, we investigated the effect of BPDE on human induced pluripotent stem cells (hiPSCs) and their differentiated neural progenitor cells (NPCs) as a model of early embryonic development. Furthermore, we compared hiPSCs and NPCs derived from patient suffering from Nijmegen Breakage Syndrome (NBS), which is a chromosomal instability disorder characterized by defective DNA repair and increased risk of malignancies. Transcriptome and selected protein analysis indicated that hiPSCs compared to NPCs are more sensitive to BPDE exposure. The affected biological processes included p53-mediated DNA damage response, DNA repair by lesion bypass, cell cycle checkpoints and extrinsic apoptosis. In addition, NBS-derived cells exhibited a reduced apoptotic response and a distinct p53 response compared their healthy counterparts. Overall, this iPSC-based model provides insights into the cellular responses to BPDE during early human development in both healthy individuals and NBS patients.

title: Interprofessional simulation-based training for obstetric and neonatal emergencies: a systematic review
abstractText: Background Co-ordinated multidisciplinary response is essential in managing delivery room emergencies, though many current simulation initiatives remain single-profession or focus on separate care streams. While interprofessional simulation-based training (IP SBT) programmes have been increasingly adopted to improve team performance, this systematic review provides the first global evaluation of its prevalence, structure and effectiveness across Kirkpatrick-level outcomes. By examining participant perceptions, clinical knowledge and patient/organization-level outcomes, this review identifies critical structural gaps to guide the future development of integrated maternal-neonatal emergency programmes. Methods Systematic search and data extraction followed PRISMA guidelines. A total of 7473 studies were identified through PubMed, EMBASE, CINAHL and MEDLINE databases (updated March 2026). Forty studies from 18 countries fulfilled inclusion criteria. All included simulation of both obstetric and neonatal emergencies involving at least two healthcare professions. Risk of bias was assessed using ROBINS-I and JBI tools, and certainty of evidence was assessed using GRADE criteria. Results Programmes varied in structure and high-technology use, with postpartum haemorrhage (n = 27), shoulder dystocia (n = 25) and neonatal resuscitation (n = 22) being the most frequently simulated scenarios. Only 12.5% of studies (n = 5) specifically simulated concurrent maternal-neonatal emergencies requiring simultaneous resuscitation. Outcome synthesis using the Kirkpatrick hierarchy demonstrated widespread improvements in participant reactions (n = 17), clinical knowledge (n = 23) and teamwork/communication behaviours (n = 15). Organizational outcomes (n = 7) included identification of latent safety threats and equipment preparedness, whilst patient-level outcomes included a 21% reduction in Caesarean section rates and up to a 34% decrease in neonatal mortality and intrapartum stillbirth. The overall certainty of evidence was moderate. Conclusion Limited, heterogeneous evidence suggests that IP SBT for delivery room emergencies positively influenced team performance and clinical proficiency. This review identifies a major structural gap in simulation design, with only 12.5% (n = 5) simulating the concurrent resuscitation of both mother and newborn. While widespread improvements were noted in teamwork, communication and clinical knowledge, evidence linking simulation to sustained clinical translation and patient outcomes remains sparse. Future research should investigate optimal scenario sequencing (simultaneous vs. sequential), evaluate the effectiveness of emerging online and blended delivery models, and focus on longitudinal evaluation of patient-level impacts.

title: Fat cadherin cleavage releases a nuclear fragment to regulate gene transcription
abstractText: Abstract Atypical Fat (Ft) cadherins regulate growth, planar cell polarity (PCP), and metabolism, in organisms ranging from flies to mammals. The intracellular domain of the Ft protein, FtICD, regulates components of the Hippo and PCP pathways at the apical-junctional plasma membrane. Unexpectedly, we find that a fragment of FtICD is imported into the nucleus and identify two conserved nuclear localization signals. Membrane-bound FtICD is cleaved and enters nuclei in vivo, and endogenous ChIP-seq experiments identified putative Ft targets, including genes involved in signaling pathways, chromatin organization and pattern formation. Ectopic expression of FtICD suppresses wing growth, alters PCP and alters the expression of many genes. FtICD forms a complex with the Hippo transcriptional effectors Scalloped and Yorkie, and Ft ChIP-seq peaks co-localize with those of Scalloped and Yorkie. We propose that modulation of Hippo pathway activity and PCP constitute nuclear functions of Ft, complementing its established function as an upstream regulator of Hippo signaling.

title: Fixel-based analysis identifies selective vulnerability of non-dominant fiber populations in aging and mild cognitive impairment
abstractText: Abstract Fixel-based analysis (FBA) resolves fiber-specific white matter properties within crossing-fiber regions, where conventional diffusion tensor imaging is limited. We applied single-shell three-tissue constrained spherical deconvolution to diffusion MRI from 295 older adults in the Vanderbilt Memory and Aging Project cohort, quantifying fiber density (FD), fiber-bundle cross-section (FC), and their composite (FDC) across the primary (N1), secondary (N2), and tertiary (N3) fiber populations within each white matter voxel. White matter was stratified into crossing-fiber complexity strata defined by the number of distinct bundles per voxel, and covariate-adjusted models examined associations with age, cognitive status, and cognition. FC declined with age most steeply in the non-dominant fiber populations. In these populations, FC was lower in participants with mild cognitive impairment than in cognitively unimpaired participants, and higher FC was associated with better executive function. The age-related decline in non-dominant FC did not vary across crossing-fiber complexity, indicating that fiber-population identity, rather than local architecture, organizes age-related vulnerability. FD and FDC showed age associations that became more positive as complexity increased, with the N1 FD association reversing from negative in the least complex regions to positive in the most complex. This behavior is consistent with how density is estimated in multi-fiber voxels rather than with fiber loss, identifying FC as the more interpretable metric in crossing-fiber regions. These findings identify fiber cross-section in the non-dominant fiber populations as a sensitive marker of white matter aging and cognitive status and provide a framework for fiber-specific analysis in existing single-shell cohorts.

title: Amyloid pathology compresses dynamic range and degrades spatial coding in an Alzheimer’s mouse model
abstractText: Abstract Alzheimer’s disease (AD) disrupts neural circuits vital for memory and cognition. Using two-photon calcium imaging in behaving 5xFAD mice, we examined how amyloid pathology alters hippocampal CA1 activity and spatial coding. We found elevated baseline activity but reduced locomotion-driven firing, leading to a diminished neuronal dynamic range. To our knowledge, this is the first direct experimental evidence for reduced dynamic range in an AD model. These abnormalities were strongest near amyloid plaques and became more widespread with age. We also observed altered network synchrony, degraded spatial coding, and increased neuronal response variability. Furthermore, place fields emerged more slowly in both familiar and novel environments, indicating impaired recall and learning. By showing a link between local plaque pathology and impaired flexible modulation of CA1 activity and progressive deficits in spatial memory coding, our study offers new insights into the circuit basis of cognitive decline in AD.

title: Facilitators and barriers to the implementation of community-based medication adherence support for aging individuals with HIV and hypertension in Western Kenya
abstractText: Background: The advent of antiretroviral therapy (ART) remarkably improved the longevity and quality of life of people living with HIV (PLWH). However, as PLWH age, they often experience comorbidities, necessitating multiple medications, resulting in increased medication adherence challenges. Patient-tailored community-based medication adherence programs can improve adherence in this population. We explored facilitators of and barriers to the implementation of community health volunteer (CHV)-led medication adherence (CBA) support programs for older people living with HIV (OALWH). Methods: This qualitative study involved 166 purposefully sampled participants. In-depth interviews (IDIs) were held with 27 healthcare providers (HCPs), 28 CHVs, and 25 older adults' caregivers. Six focus group discussions (FGDs) were held with 86 OALWH affiliated with three health facilities in western Kenya. The IDIs and FGDs covered topics on perceived barriers and facilitators to having a CHV visit OALWH's home to offer medication adherence support. The data were analyzed thematically and organized using the Consolidated Framework for Implementation Research (CFIR). Results: The findings revealed various factors that could influence the implementation of a CBA intervention for OALWH and hypertension. Facilitators included the relative advantage and adaptability of the intervention, the enhanced collaboration between facility and community care providers, and the potential to promote patient-centered care. However, participants voiced several factors that may impede the intervention, such as the complexity of the intervention, increased workload and costs for CHVs, limited knowledge of hypertension management, unmet patient needs, and limited health financing for NCD medications. Fears of decreased cognitive ability, low cardiovascular risk perception, and medication side effects among OALWH were perceived to pose challenges. Furthermore, trust and empathy between CHVs and patients were identified as critical personal attributes that foster patient empowerment. Conclusion: This study identified barriers, highlighting the complexities of tailoring community support services to the needs of OALWH. The findings underscore the necessity for a holistic, multidimensional approach to addressing medication adherence by providing OALWH with the requisite hypertension management messaging, revisiting health system barriers (NCD care financing), and facilitating CHVs with knowledge, skills, and remuneration to enable them to efficiently support CBA intervention.

title: Microbial peptidoglycan activates mitophagy via binding autophagy adaptor p62 to reduce liver fibrosis
abstractText: Abstract Mitophagy is critical for maintaining mitochondrial integrity and liver homeostasis, yet the specific microbial signals that regulate this process are poorly defined. Here, we identify bacterial peptidoglycan (PGN), a ubiquitous component of the bacterial cell wall, as a microbial signal that activates hepatocyte mitophagy and protects against liver fibrosis. PGN is internalized by hepatocytes and associates with mitochondria, where it engages the autophagic adaptor p62 (SQSTM1) to promote mitophagy. Hepatocyte-specific loss of p62 completely abolished PGN-induced mitophagy, establishing p62 as an essential mediator of this microbial response. Functionally, PGN-induced mitophagy protected hepatocytes from drug-induced cell death in vitro and in vivo, PGN administration reduced collagen deposition and hepatic stellate cell activation in a CCL 4 -induced model of liver fibrosis. These findings reveal a direct functional link between a bacterial cell-wall component and hepatocyte mitochondrial quality control, uncovering a previously unrecognized gut microbiota–mitophagy axis. Thus, PGN-mediated activation of hepatocyte mitophagy represents a potential strategy for restoring mitochondrial homeostasis and limiting fibrotic liver injury.

title: Optimal backwashing rate range in sand media filters for microirrigation systems
abstractText: Appropriate backwashing rates are essential to maintain sand media filter performance, as they enable the effective removal of retained impurities without compromising the integrity of the filter bed. This study evaluated the relationship between backwashing rate, bed expansion, and solids removal efficiency in a pressurised sand filter prototype, aiming to identify an optimal operational backwashing range and assess the applicability of the conventional 25% bed expansion criterion. Experimental results indicated that maximum solids removal occurs before the bed reaches 25% expansion, and that rates above 160 m 3 m −2 h −1 result in substantial loss of filter material. A backwashing rate range of 52.90-88.17 m 3 m −2 h −1 was identified as the optimal operational range, considering solids removal efficiency, filter bed expansion, and water consumption. Within this range, solids removal efficiency reached approximately 99.8% at 88.17 m 3 m −2 h −1 , with negligible additional improvements at higher backwashing rates. The comparison between the commercial filter and the sand filter prototype demonstrated similar behaviour up to 140 m 3 m −2 h −1 , indicating that the values obtained with the prototype can be extrapolated to applications in commercial filters. These findings offer the opportunity to establish more accurate guidelines for determining backwashing rates in sand media filters. While the results are most representative of the tested prototype and sand media characteristics, the proposed methodology provides a basis for future studies involving different filter media and filter configurations to further refine and generalise these findings.

title: Mode‐specific fetal heart rate signal dropout as a marker of perinatal asphyxia: A multicenter observational study using causal machine learning methods
abstractText: Abstract Objective Cardiotocography (CTG) is the standard method for intrapartum fetal monitoring. Modern systems acquire fetal heart rate (FHR) using external Doppler ultrasound (US) or internal fetal scalp electrocardiography (ECG). We evaluated whether mode‐specific FHR signal dropout was associated with perinatal asphyxia and whether it should be retained as an informative, mode‐aware feature for downstream predictive models. Methods We conducted a retrospective multicenter cohort study using routinely collected clinical and CTG data from Mercy Hospital for Women, Melbourne, Australia, for 2010–2021; Werribee Mercy Hospital, Melbourne, Australia, for 2010–2021; and the Czech CTU‐UHB database from University Hospital Brno, for 2010–2012. A total of 46 662 labor episodes at ≥36 weeks' gestation with ≥15 min of interpretable CTG data in the final 60 min before birth were analyzed (32 242 in the model‐development cohort, 548 in the Czech validation cohort, and 13 872 in the Australian community validation cohort). The exposure was mode‐specific FHR dropout, classified as US low dropout, US high dropout (>30%), ECG low dropout, or ECG high dropout (>30%). The primary outcome was sustained perinatal asphyxia, defined using a Delphi‐consensus composite of clinical, biochemical, and neurologic criteria. Results In the model‐development cohort, 860 cases of perinatal asphyxia occurred (2.67%, 95% CI 2.49%–2.85%). Compared with US low dropout, ECG high dropout was associated with higher risk of asphyxia (inverse probability weighting IPW‐adjusted odds ratio [OR] 3.14, 95% CI 2.20–4.48; targeted maximum likelihood estimation‐adjusted OR 2.08, 95% CI 1.21–3.58), corresponding to an absolute risk increase of 2.27% (one additional case per 44 births). Survival analysis supported elevated hazards (HR 4.76, 95% CI 2.98–7.62). External validation supported the direction of association, although estimates varied across cohorts. Conclusion In retrospective multicenter analyses, high FHR dropout during ECG monitoring was associated with increased perinatal asphyxia risk. These findings support evaluating mode‐specific dropout as an informative signal‐quality feature in future predictive models. Prospective validation of such models is needed before clinical implementation.

title: Ragnarok: A flexible and RApid GeNe annotation (ROcKs) pipeline deployed through Nextflow
abstractText: Abstract High‐quality genome assemblies and pan‐genomes are increasingly achievable and accessible due to advances in third‐generation sequencing and assembly algorithms, but genome annotation remains a critical bottleneck. Existing gene annotation pipelines often require complex installations, multiple steps, and long runtimes and produce variable results, which impede quality and the downstream usage of the annotations. We developed RAGNAROK (RApid GeNe Annotation ROcKs), a modular annotation pipeline built on Nextflow and Apptainer that integrates ab initio prediction, transcriptome and protein evidence, repeat annotation, functional assignment, and quality assessment into a single reproducible workflow for plant genomes. Moreover, RAGNAROK utilizes graphical processing unit acceleration and parallelization of select processes to decrease the time required to produce high‐quality gene annotation. We benchmarked against BRAKER3 across seven diverse, reference‐quality plant genomes and demonstrated that when including untranslated region (UTR) features, RAGNAROK achieved higher sensitivity, precision, and F1 scores at the exon, transcript, and gene levels. Furthermore, we demonstrated RAGNAROK's improvement in re‐annotating a suite of five Rosaceae genomes that were previously annotated using MAKER. Overall, RAGNAROK produced more ideal mono:multi‐exonic gene ratios, improved benchmarking of universal single‐copy orthologs completeness scores, and reduced missing gene content compared to other pipelines. Additionally, RAGNAROK consistently outperformed BRAKER3 in overall runtime, scaling efficiently from small to gigabase‐scale genomes. RAGNAROK provides a flexible, rapid, scalable, and accurate solution for de novo (first attempt or without prior evidence) and re‐annotation of plant genomes. Its modular design and workflow scalability lay the foundation for future extensions to animal, fungal, and other eukaryotic genomes. RAGNAROK is available at https://github.com/ryandkuster/ragnarok .

title: Effect of scour on dynamic response within the fine sand seabed around a monopile foundation under wave action
abstractText: Offshore wind power, a renewable energy, effectively alleviates global energy pressure. Monopile foundation, known for its technical maturity, low cost, and rapid construction, is the predominant foundation type for offshore wind turbines. Seabed response and scour evolution around monopile foundations are critical factors affecting their operational safety. Therefore, this study investigates the local scour evolution and its influence on wave-induced dynamic response within a fine-sand seabed around a monopile through physical model tests. Effects of wave height, wave period, and water depth on the spatial-temporal distribution of scour topography and pore pressure response around the pile are investigated. Results indicate that the development of scour pit modifies the local flow field and soil stress state, leading to a non-monotonic trend in the pore pressure response within seabed, which initially increases then decreases and finally recovers gradually. Increasing wave height and wave period enhances both the scour and pore pressure response, while greater water depth reduces the blockage effect of pile, mitigating scour and decreasing pore pressure amplitude. This study reveals the dynamic mechanism of scour evolution on seabed response, providing important theoretical and technical support for the design and safety assessment of monopile foundations in offshore wind power engineering.

title: Implementation and evaluation of evidence-based intrahospital transport guidelines for critically ill children: a multi-framework implementation study using i-PARIHS and RE-AIM
abstractText: Intrahospital transport of critically ill children is a high-risk process requiring standardized risk assessment, team coordination, equipment preparation, and structured handover. Despite the availability of evidence-based clinical practice guidelines, translating recommendations into routine clinical practice remains a persistent challenge. To implement selected recommendations from the 2023 Clinical Practice Guidelines for Intrahospital Transport of Hospitalized Children into ED-to-PICU transport practice at a tertiary pediatric center, and to evaluate the implementation process and outcomes using the RE-AIM framework. A single-center, quasi-experimental before–after implementation study was conducted at Shenzhen Children’s Hospital. Barriers and facilitators were assessed through semi-structured interviews, questionnaire surveys, and field observations guided by the i-PARIHS framework, and targeted implementation strategies were developed accordingly. Provider knowledge was assessed before and after implementation. Outcomes were assessed by comparing prospectively observed transport events at baseline ( n = 76) and follow-up ( n = 78), with evaluation organized across the RE-AIM dimensions of reach, effectiveness, adoption, implementation, and preliminary maintenance. Of 64 eligible healthcare providers, 62 (96.5%) participated in the implementation program. Provider knowledge scores improved significantly (60.36 ± 11.42 vs. 79.53 ± 11.25; p < 0.001). Protocol adherence improved significantly in 9 of 15 audit indicators: five newly introduced criteria increased from 0% to 100%, while the remaining four reflected existing practices that were further strengthened to full adherence. All planned implementation strategies were fully executed. Transport-related adverse events were less frequent during follow-up than at baseline (1/78 [1.28%] vs. 12/76 [15.79%]). This exploratory finding should be interpreted cautiously because of the short observation period, small number of events, potential regression to the mean, secular changes, and unmeasured confounding inherent in the pre–post design. A theory-informed, multi-strategy implementation program was associated with improvements in provider knowledge and protocol adherence in pediatric intrahospital transport. Multicenter studies with longer follow-up are needed to confirm the sustainability and generalizability of these findings.

title: Benchmarking AI-evolved cosmological structure formation
abstractText: Abstract The potential of deep learning-based image-to-image translations has attracted significant attention as a fast, approximate alternative to cosmological simulations, which would be particularly useful in various contexts, including covariance studies, investigations of systematics, and cosmological parameter inference. We model the evolution of structure formation using U-Net, a widely employed convolutional image translation framework with previous applications in cosmology. To study aspects of learning-based cosmological mappings in a controlled, illustrative setting, we use two approaches for generating suitable cosmological matter fields as datasets: a simple analytical prescription provided by the Zel’dovich approximation, and a standard N-body method using Particle-Mesh simulations. We apply established metrics such as matter power spectra and bispectra, topological indicators, and statistical independence of density fields and study their reproducibility and convergence properties. The U-Net approach performs well only for some of these physical metrics, and accuracy is worse at more nonlinear scales, where the dynamic range in density is larger. Motivated by field-level emulator studies utilizing Eulerian-aware loss functions and beyond pixel-wise mean squared errors, we examine a density-weighted objective. In the PM tests ending at z = 4, where the evolution is only mildly nonlinear, using the Eulerian matter density evaluated at each particle position as a direct weight on that particle’s Lagrangian displacement error improves the U-Net results at smaller scales; this result does not establish comparable accuracy in the strongly nonlinear low-redshift regime.

title: MRI of ASCT2-mediated amino acid uptake in xenograft tumor models
abstractText: Abstract Alanine-serine-cysteine transporter 2 (ASCT2) is a prognostic marker for many cancers. While histological expression is the current clinical metric for ASCT2 evaluation, expression does not scale with activity because post-translational modifications are required for translocation to the plasma membrane. Methods to trace ASCT2 activity ex vivo have not been developed and commercialized. We investigated the utility of imaging alanine as a biomarker for ASCT2 in cancer. Alanine is a major ASCT2 substrate that can be detected in magnetic resonance imaging (MRI) scanners using the chemical exchange saturation transfer (CEST) method. Initially, we demonstrated that its CEST contrast was higher than other major ASCT2 substrates at physiological pH (7.3). We then investigated the sensitivity of alanine-weighted CEST (ALAwCEST) imaging to ASCT2 in vivo using a genetically-engineered patient-derived pancreatic cancer model that we developed. ASCT2 protein expression at the cell surface was 1.6-fold higher in SLC1A5 -overexpressing Pa20c cells than naïve Pa20c cells ( p = 0.0221). Upon bolus injection of alanine (6 mmol/kg i.v.) in tumor-bearing mice, CEST MRI enhancement was higher in SLC1A5 -overexpressing Pa20c tumors than naïve tumors ( p < 0.0001). We next investigated the feasibility of ALAwCEST to distinguish prostate tumors with differing levels of ASCT2 content. Enhancement upon injection of 13 C3-alanine was more pronounced in LNCaP prostate tumors than DU-145 prostate tumors in vivo ( p < 0.0001). Notably, the temporal dynamics of ALAwCEST signal enhancement depended on the volume of the tumor. Mass spectrometric imaging of 13 C-labeled metabolites and CEST imaging of metabolite phantoms revealed these differences in in vivo dynamics could be attributed to differences in alanine uptake and metabolism. Overall, we demonstrated the feasibility of ALAwCEST imaging for reporting ASCT2-mediated amino acid uptake in multiple human xenograft tumor models and its utility for cancer applications.

title: A gap-free telomere-to-telomere pig reference genome provides insights into Eurasian pig diversity
abstractText: Abstract The domestic pig is a key agricultural species and biomedical model, yet its reference genome has remained incomplete. Using PacBio HiFi, Oxford Nanopore reads, and Hi-C sequencing, we assembled the first telomere-to-telomere (T2T), gap-free pig genome (T2T-Sscrofa). Importantly, this assembly derives from the same individual pig that provided the original reference genome, thereby completing the long-standing foundation of pig genomics. This assembly resolves 274.8 Mb of previously unassembled sequence, including centromeres, segmental duplications, and ribosomal DNA arrays, and identifies 255 new protein-coding genes. Comparative analyses reveal a Robertsonian translocation in the western European wild boar and extensive structural variation across global pig populations. T2T-Sscrofa provides a comprehensive genomic foundation for agricultural, evolutionary, and biomedical research.

title: Single cell RNA sequencing reveals unexpected heterogeneity and identifies AP2XI-6 as a mature bradyzoite specific cell cycle regulator
abstractText: Toxoplasma gondii prevalence is due, in part, to its ability to persist in hosts while retaining the capacity to transmit and recrudesce. This process, while critical, is poorly understood. Through single cell RNA profiling of in vivo-derived bradyzoites, we show that bradyzoites are heterogeneous and not G1-arrested, as expected from in vitro studies. Instead, they progress through two distinct cell cycles that branch from a single G1 state. One is common amongst tachyzoites and in vitro- and in vivo-derived bradyzoites; the other is newly identified within the population of in vivo-derived bradyzoites. While in G1b, these in vivo-derived bradyzoites express cyst wall proteins predicted to replenish the wall that protects cysts and prevents clearance. We demonstrate that AP2XI-6, a putative AP2-transcription factor expressed by bradyzoites in G1 in vivo, is dispensable for tachyzoite growth and cyst formation in vitro but necessary for encystation or persistence in vivo. We propose that AP2XI-6 is a driver of replication through the newly identified in vivo bradyzoite specific cell cycle and that this is required for cyst maturation or persistence. Authors show mature chronic-stage T. gondii adopt cell-cycle-controlled cyst-wall protein expression and two cell-cycle architectures in vivo. AP2XI-6 is required for the mature architecture; without it, parasites form cysts in vitro but fail in vivo.

title: Hierarchical importance sampling for estimating occupation time for SDE solutions
abstractText: Abstract This study considers the estimation of the complementary cumulative distribution function of the occupation time (i.e., the time spent below a threshold) for a process governed by a stochastic differential equation. The focus is on the right tail, where the underlying event becomes rare, and using variance reduction techniques is essential to obtain computationally efficient estimates. Building on recent developments that relate importance sampling (IS) to stochastic optimal control, this work develops an optimal single-level IS (SLIS) estimator based on the solution of an auxiliary Hamilton–Jacobi–Bellman (HJB) partial differential equation (PDE). The cost of solving the HJB-PDE is incorporated into the total computational work, and an optimized trade-off between preprocessing and sampling is proposed to minimize the overall cost. The SLIS approach is extended to the multilevel setting to enhance efficiency, yielding a multilevel IS (MLIS) estimator. Motivated by the zero-variance property of the ideal full-state continuous-time control, we study regimes in which the single-level variance decreases with refinement; this decay is assessed numerically for the implemented approximate control. This observation leads to the formulation of a necessary condition and a sufficient condition under which MLIS outperforms SLIS. To promote satisfaction of the sufficient condition, we introduce a smoothing of both the drift and the observable to enhance the variance decay rate, together with a novel common-likelihood MLIS formulation that is observed numerically to preserve this decay under IS. The classical multilevel Monte Carlo complexity theory can be extended to accommodate settings in which the variance on coarse levels depends on the target accuracy, a phenomenon for which the variance-decay behavior in the IS setting is a key example. Notably, the sampling work complexity of MLIS can be better than quadratic. Numerical experiments on fade-duration estimation demonstrate the effectiveness of the proposed approach and validate the theoretical analysis. In particular, the smoothing bias is estimated to be negligible relative to the prescribed tolerances, while the common-likelihood MLIS estimator achieves a substantial reduction in computational cost compared with SLIS.

title: Dynamic spatio-temporal sequential ordinal models: Application to invasive weeds
abstractText: Abstract The multivariate sequential ordinal model is investigated for use in the Bayesian analysis of spatio-temporal ordinal data. The sequential ordinal model likelihood is equivalent to a binary model conditional on unknown regression coefficients and spatio-temporal random effects. Therefore estimation and prediction in the space-time context can proceed using the well-established dynamic generalised linear model framework. Moreover, the sequential ordinal model avoids the ordering constraints on the threshold parameters that determine the category break points required by cumulative ordinal models, and so simplifies the estimation procedure for high-dimensional space-time applications using Bayesian inference. The dynamic spatio-temporal sequential ordinal model is applied to estimate the cover-abundance of four invasive alien weed species. These weeds are observed by means of a modified Braun-Blanquet score that is commonly used in vegetation studies and constitutes ordinal data. As all four weeds are actively managed, the multivariate ordinal data are sparsely distributed in space and time with few observations recorded in high cover-abundance categories. A separable model for space-time dependence that maintains parameter interpretability in the presence of aggregated ordinal categories is therefore developed and applied to each species of interest. The dynamic spatio-temporal sequential ordinal model is shown to be particularly useful for biological populations. Estimation and prediction is demonstrated using integrated nested Laplace approximation (INLA) methods developed for univariate spatio-temporal models. Bayesian estimation and prediction shows that the four invasive weed species differentially respond to habitat type, control effort and accessibility, and share similar magnitudes of dependence with short effective spatial ranges and strong temporal autocorrelations.

title: Nanoclay-enhanced shear thinning gelatin/alginate hydrogels with tunable physicochemical properties for cytocompatible scaffolds
abstractText: The development of cytocompatible hydrogels with tunable mechanical and degradation properties is important for cell growth and tissue-mimetic scaffolds. This study fabricated and characterized gelatin/alginate hydrogels containing 0, 1, and 2 wt% laponite to evaluate their potential for cell-based applications. Their morphological, mechanical, physicochemical, and biological properties were assessed using FTIR, XRD, SEM, swelling and degradation analyses, compression and rheological testing, MTT assay, and cell attachment studies. Laponite incorporation reduced the average pore size in freeze-dried SEM cross-sections from 46 ± 9 μm for Lap 0% to 42 ± 8 μm and 26 ± 7 μm for Lap 1% and Lap 2%, respectively. Compared with Lap 0%, the 360-min swelling ratio decreased by approximately 29% for Lap 1% and 47% for Lap 2%, while the 7-day mass loss decreased from 57% to 48% and 16%, respectively. Lap 1% exhibited more than twice the compressive strength of Lap 0%, while the non-crosslinked precursor formulations exhibited shear-thinning behavior. The hydrogels maintained high hydration (> 90%) and supported L929 fibroblast metabolic activity and initial human bone marrow-derived mesenchymal stem cell (hBMSC) attachment, demonstrating cytocompatibility under the tested conditions and potential for further cell-based studies.

title: A subspecialty diagnostic system powered by self-supervised learning for cervical histopathology
abstractText: Cervical cancer remains a major malignancy in women, with large-scale human papillomavirus-based screening generating a large volume of biopsies and, for advanced cases, surgical specimens, imposing an overwhelming diagnostic burden that necessitates precise histopathological evaluation. Although deep learning shows promise, general foundation models offer a broader reach but remain limited in capturing subspecialty-specific features and task adaptability. We introduce the Cervical Subspecialty Pathology (CerS-Path) diagnostic system, built upon the subspecialized dataset and developed through two synergistic pretraining stages: self-supervised learning on approximately 190 million tissue patches to build a cervical-specific feature extractor, and multimodal enhancement with 2.5 million image-text pairs, followed by diagnostic functions integration and downstream task enhancement. CerS-Path integrates eight functions—across morphological diagnosis, predictive analytics, and multimodal tasks—to cover the diagnostic workflow from biopsies to resection specimens. Comprehensive evaluations demonstrate improved performance in cervical pathology in female patients, where CerS-Path outperforms state-of-the-art foundation models across 26 of 30 diagnostic tasks. Furthermore, in multicenter retrospective and prospective validation across six independent cohorts of women, CerS-Path achieves up to 99% sensitivity for clinically relevant lesion detection with acceptable specificity across sites, highlighting its potential for screening-derived histopathology and suitability for integration into high-volume diagnostic pathways. Foundation models could be promising for cervical cancer screening, but have important limitations for their clinical deployment. Here, the authors introduce the Cervical Subspecialty Pathology (CerS-Path) diagnostic system, a self-supervised learning framework for cervical cancer pathology that outperforms state-of-the-art foundation models across multiple diagnostic tasks.

Comparison of interventional causal structure learning algorithms for gene regulatory network inference
abstractText: Abstract Background Causal structure learning offers a promising approach to studying gene regulation in cells, aiming to provide deeper mechanistic insights than purely association-based methods. Theoretical groundwork indicating that interventions improve identifiability of causal structure motivates the use of causal structure learning methods in scenarios with interventional information. Results This benchmark investigates the ability of existing causal structure learning algorithms to leverage the information revealed by targeted interventions to infer gene regulatory networks (GRNs). In this study synthetic single-cell perturbation data and experimental data from a clustered regularly interspaced short palindromic repeats (CRISPR) screen are leveraged, and a suite of causal structure learning algorithms is evaluated on metrics tailored to synthetic ground truth and real biological data respectively. On synthetic data, accurate recovery of GRNs was achieved under favourable conditions: strong interventions, large sample sizes, and low measurement noise. For experimental data, no reliable ground truth is available, so inferred GRNs were assessed indirectly, using observed perturbation effects and curated regulatory annotations. Here, performance remained unreliable, with technical and biological noise and algorithmic scalability as limiting factors. This highlights a current gap between theoretical potential and practical application of causal structure learning for GRNs. Conclusions The benchmark provides insight into algorithm strengths and limitations and offers groundwork for further methodological development. We also provide an accessible software package for applying modern causal structure learning to custom datasets and thereby foster future exploration of its potential.

title: Targeted GC-MS profiling of 34 serum free fatty acids: analytical performance and clinical application in acute lymphoblastic leukemia
abstractText: Background Accurate quantification of free fatty acids (FFAs) in complex biological matrices in human serum is analytically challenging due to variations in carbon chain length, polarity, and volatility.Method In this study, we describe a targeted GC-MS (gas chromatography mass spectrometry) method for simultaneous profiling of 34 serum FFAs (C4-C24) spanning short-, medium-, and long-chain saturated and unsaturated fatty acids and evaluate its analytical performance and clinical applicability in ALL (Acute Lymphoblastic Leukemia). A one-step Folch extraction with Meth Prep II methylation was optimized for preparation of FAMEs (fatty acid methyl esters) and compounds were detected in selected ion monitoring (SIM) mode.Results Analytical validation showed excellent linearity across the calibration range (3.7–60 µg/mL) with coefficients of determination (R2) ranging from 0.9917 to 0.9994 across the analytes. Sub µg/mL LOD values ranged from 0.0001–0.137 µg/mL, LOQ values from 0.0003–0.457 µg/mL, and lowest calibration values from 3.3–13.85 µg/mL, corresponding to lowest calibration levels. Inter-day RSD% (precision) were ±10% across analytes, while RE% (accuracy) were within ±20%. Clinical applicability was evaluated serum samples from newly diagnosed ALL patients at baseline (N = 142) and post-induction chemotherapy (N = 123). Multivariate clustering confirmed clear separation between clinical groups.Conclusion Overall, this fit-for-purpose GC-MS profiling supports clinical metabolomics investigations of lipid dysregulation in ALL.
