title: Field-angle-resolved heat transport in UTe2: determination of nodal positions in the superconducting order parameter
abstractText: Abstract One of the recurring hurdles in studying unconventional superconductivity is the challenge of efficiently and conclusively identifying the symmetry of the superconducting order parameter in a new material. Uranium ditelluride (UTe 2 ) exhibits an unprecedented number of superconducting phases, and none of them has had its symmetry conclusively identified so far. Here we report results of an extensive study of the thermal conductivity of UTe 2 in the superconducting state as a function of the angle of an applied magnetic field rotated in the b-c plane. We observe substantial oscillations in the thermal conductivity as a function of field angle, and, utilizing the experimentally determined Fermi surface, we model this phenomenon for all potential gap structures in UTe 2 . This allows us to identify point nodes near the b-axis, implying that the superconducting order parameter most likely belongs to the B 2 u irreducible representation of the crystal point group.

title: Organelle distribution and protein translation defects in radial glia cells with mutations in Eml1
abstractText: Abstract Cerebral cortical development is a finely regulated process, depending on key neuronal progenitors, giving rise to post-mitotic neurons that migrate to superficial regions in the developing brain. Disruptions can give rise to severe cortical malformations that are associated with intellectual disability and intractable epilepsy. Mutations in EML1/Eml1 , coding for a microtubule (MT)-associated protein, lead to subcortical heterotopia (SH) in both humans and mice. In developing mutant mouse brains, ectopic apical radial glia (aRG) progenitors were found outside the normal proliferative ventricular zone (VZ). The normal role of Eml1 in these cells remains to be precisely determined. Using proteomics and imaging approaches, we compared brain tissue from control and mutant mice and identified microtubule and organelle dysregulation. Eml1 influences the trafficking of organelles to different compartments of aRG, where they may be involved in local functions. Thus, we find that mitochondrial and polysome distribution are altered in mutant conditions. Indeed, Eml1 interacts with translational machinery, and an overall downregulation of translation is observed when analysing the translatome of Eml1 mutant aRG. Paradoxically, an upregulation of translation-related mRNAs is also observed. These new data uncover an unprecedented function of Eml1, as well as associating novel subcellular patho-mechanisms with severe heterotopia formation.

Mapping Aluminum Flows in the United States Using Advanced Bayesian Material Flow Analysis
abstractText: Abstract This paper presents a Bayesian material flow analysis (MFA) of aluminum in the U.S. economy, reconciling a 2017 baseline and updating the system through 2022. We introduce ARCADE (Abiotic Resource Cycles, Allocations, and Dynamics in the Economy), a unified Bayesian MFA framework integrating system definition, data pedigree, and probabilistic reconciliation under physical constraints. ARCADE combines government statistics, trade records, and industry reports into a physically consistent network and reports uncertainty-aware metrics. Results show continued U.S. reliance on imports of unwrought and finished aluminum products. The posterior median end-of-life (EOL) collection rate was 66.8% [57.2%, 79.9%] in 2017 and 67.6% [62.3%, 73.9%] in 2022. Median domestic retention of collected EOL scrap was lower in 2022 (52.7% [49.6%, 55.6%]) than in 2017 (56.4% [51.7%, 60.5%]), although the credible interval for the change spanned zero. Across robustness cases varying source weighting, pedigree-to-uncertainty mappings, and prior strength, domestic retention remained below 60%. Spatial analysis identified mismatches between EOL scrap generation and domestic remelting capacity. These findings show that improved collection alone may not increase domestic recycling when processing constraints persist. We observe a continued import dependence, efficient circulation of prompt fabrication scrap, and limited domestic retention of collected EOL scrap.

title: Geological constraints on bunker-buster penetration at Iran’s Fordow facility and implications for media reporting
abstractText: Media reports on the June 2025 US strike against Iran’s Fordow nuclear facility during the “12-Day War” frequently cited the GBU-57 bunker-buster’s “200-foot penetration capability” without clarifying the source, material conditions, or geological assumptions underlying that figure. This study assesses whether open-source geoscientific data can support independent technical scrutiny of the claim and its application to the Fordow strike. This article applies a geojournalistic, open-source approach integrating commercial satellite imagery, regional geological studies, and empirical measurements of rock compressive strength from Iran’s Central Domain. These sources are used to locate the facility, characterise the likely target geology, and compare regional rock strength with the material conditions attached to publicly reported penetration figures. Publicly available sources do not establish 200 feet as a verified and generally transferable penetration capability. A 2005 Congressional Record linked the figure of 60 m to reinforced concrete rated at 5,000 pounds per square inch (psi), but the underlying technical evidence remains unidentified. Regional studies indicate heterogeneous sedimentary and igneous rock masses, with mean sample strengths near 10,000 psi. The penetration depth achieved at Fordow may therefore have been substantially less than the widely cited 200-foot figure. Although definitive damage assessment requires classified disclosure or on-site inspection, meaningful technical scrutiny is possible using open-source geoscientific data. Reporting maximum penetration figures without their evidentiary and material qualifications risks overstating the weapon’s performance and distorting public understanding.

title: Structural brain changes in age-related macular degeneration before and 6 months after Scharioth macula lens implantation: an exploratory MRI study
abstractText: Abstract Background and purpose Age-related macular degeneration (AMD) is associated with visual impairment and with structural and functional brain differences. The extent of these differences and whether longitudinal structural changes are detectable after visual rehabilitation, including implantation of the Scharioth macula lens (SML), remain incompletely understood. This study aimed primarily to characterize baseline deviations from normative MRI reference values and secondarily to describe whether longitudinal changes were detectable after SML implantation. Materials and methods Ten patients with dry AMD (mean age 78.8 ± 5.6 years) underwent structural brain MRI at 3 T before and 6 months after SML implantation. Regional volumes and age-, sex-, and head-size-normalized normative percentiles were generated using the fully automated AI-assisted multi-atlas segmentation tool (cNeuro cMRI). All reported hypothesis tests used normative percentiles; absolute regional volumes were not used in inferential analyses. Analyses included baseline deviation in an anatomically defined visual-network family (k = 36), exploratory longitudinal visual-network tests (k = 36), an exploratory analysis outside that network (k = 221), and an exploratory reduced-dimension family of three brain and three quality-of-life (VFQ-25) composites (k = 6), with false discovery rate (FDR) correction within each family. Results At baseline, deviation from the normative median survived FDR correction for the left, total, and right occipital pole and the left lingual gyrus. Longitudinal visual-network observations were limited to uncorrected exploratory changes in the left middle occipital gyrus (p = 0.004, pFDR = 0.141), total occipital pole (p = 0.027, pFDR = 0.428), and left occipital lobe (p = 0.049, pFDR = 0.428); none survived FDR correction. No region outside the visual network survived FDR correction (minimum pFDR = 0.216). None of the six reduced-dimension composites survived FDR correction, and no exploratory structure–function association or regression coefficient was robust after correction or interval estimation. Conclusions Patients with dry AMD showed regionally selective structural deviations in the posterior visual cortex, particularly the occipital pole, relative to the normative MRI reference. No longitudinal finding within or outside the visual network survived FDR correction; the uncorrected regional observations were heterogeneous and are considered exploratory. Because the study was sensitive only to large within-subject effects, the absence of corrected structural change should be interpreted in the context of limited sensitivity and not as evidence that structural change was absent.

title: Modelling the drivers of modular construction adoption in Australia: a hybrid interpretive and classification approach
abstractText: Modular construction (MC) is increasingly promoted in Australia as a pathway toward more sustainable and efficient building delivery; however, adoption remains limited because the conditions shaping implementation are not yet fully understood. Existing studies largely identify or rank adoption drivers independently, with limited integration of hierarchical structural modelling and data-driven classification in the Australian context. This study investigates drivers of MC uptake through a mixed-method approach integrating qualitative evidence with quantitative modelling. A targeted literature scan and semi-structured interviews with 15 professionals, 11 based in Australia and four New Zealand-based comparative experts produced and refined an inventory of 79 drivers. Interview-occurrence analysis and category-specific Pareto evaluation prioritised the drivers; TISM-MICMAC modelled relationships among eight categories; and an ANN assessed how consistently occurrence and structural attributes reproduced the Pareto-defined classification. Social, technological, and supply-chain considerations occupied the strongest structural positions. A five-member content-review panel drawn from the remaining survey volunteer pool provided favourable ratings on 27 of 30 item responses (90%), with item-level favourable proportions of 60–100%. This supports face and content credibility only. Because the framework was developed from one small purposive dataset and the classifier target was occurrence-derived, the computational results remain internal-consistency evidence rather than independent causal or predictive validation.

title: Nash equilibria as limits of approximate equilibria of finite games
abstractText: Abstract We study finite-player normal-form games with compact metric action spaces and bounded Borel measurable payoffs, which need not be continuous. Our main theorem shows that every Nash equilibrium of such a game can be recovered as the limit, in the product weak topology, of $$\varepsilon _n$$ ε n -Nash equilibria of finite restrictions of the game, where $$\varepsilon _n\downarrow 0$$ ε n ↓ 0 and each restriction discretizes the action spaces without changing payoffs. For each player, the finite action sets become dense in the original action space, and the approximating sequence may depend on the prescribed equilibrium. The proof samples from the prescribed equilibrium and uses concentration inequalities to select a realization that approximates it while nearly satisfying all players’ incentive constraints simultaneously. A uniformly vanishing payoff perturbation also makes the constructed profiles exact Nash equilibria of nearby finite games. We provide an example of a continuous game showing that exact equilibria of the unperturbed finite restrictions need not suffice: the game has a Nash equilibrium that is not the limit of Nash equilibria along any sequence of such restrictions.

title: The pancreatic cancer secretome activates the STAT3 signaling in pancreatic stellate cells to drive the secretion of muscle atrophy-inducing factors
abstractText: Abstract The pancreatic tumor microenvironment, a major component of pancreatic tumors, plays important roles in tumor progression, metastasis, and chemotherapy resistance. In patients with advanced pancreatic cancer, unintentional weight loss by muscle and/or adipose tissue atrophy, called cancer cachexia, is frequently observed. Although it is well established that cancer cells secrete muscle atrophy-inducing factors, we investigated whether cancer cells also produce factors to facilitate the ability of microenvironmental cells to confer an atrophic phenotype. To test this possibility, pancreatic stellate cells were treated with conditioned medium (CCM) from various pancreatic cancer cells. We revealed that CCM from cancer cells consistently activated STAT3 to induce an atrophic phenotype in stellate cells and that this induction was not observed when CCM from brefeldin A (BFA)-treated cancer cells was added. These results suggest that conventionally secreted factors from cancer cells are responsible for the acquisition of an atrophic phenotype in stellate cells. On the other hand, BFA did not inhibit the secretion of muscle atrophy-inducing factors from either pancreatic cancer cells or stimulated stellate cells. We therefore propose that not only conventionally, but also unconventionally secreted factors contribute to muscle atrophy.

title: Oasis en Tensión: Transformación Histórica y Cambio Ambiental en un Humedal Protegido del Oeste Argentino desde el Siglo XX
abstractText: This research analyzes how historical transformations in the society–water relationship contributed to the environmental degradation of the wetland system of the Ramsar site Guanacache, Desaguadero, and Bebedero Lagoons, located in the arid center-west of Argentina, with particular emphasis from the 20th century to the present. Based on the study of the regional water balance, environmental flows, and climate change scenarios, the research examines how the expansion of irrigated oases and the territorial reorganization of water resources progressively altered the hydrosocial equilibrium of the system. Likewise, the historical context and the territorial organization linked to the balance that sustained the lacustrine system were analyzed, together with the dynamics of water use, considering both natural inputs and extractions derived from human activities. The results show that water overexploitation, combined with climate variability, compromises the sustainability of the system and generates increasing imbalances in the regional water balance, projecting scenarios of greater water stress. Additionally, the study incorporated the perspective of the Brisbane Declaration on Environmental Flows (2018) and the warnings presented in the IPCC Sixth Assessment Report (2021), both of which emphasize the need to preserve these flows in order to maintain the ecological functionality and ecosystem services of wetlands. The combined analysis reveals that the oasis, historically shaped by the interaction between society and water, is currently facing a critical situation in which agricultural, urban, and industrial demand exceeds natural supply, while projected reductions in water availability increase the system’s vulnerability. The study highlights the importance of recognizing wetlands as spaces of environmental memory and as laboratories for understanding long-term transformations in the society–water relationship, while underscoring the urgency of implementing integrated water management and climate adaptation policies.

title: Comparative prognostic performance of FIB-4, AIP, and TyG for all-cause and cardiovascular mortality in FLI-defined MASLD: a nationally representative NHANES 2011–2018 cohort study
abstractText: Abstract Background Metabolic dysfunction-associated steatotic liver disease (MASLD) is driven by both fibrosis and cardiometabolic dysfunction, but the relative prognostic value of fibrosis- and metabolism-related indices for near-term mortality remains uncertain. Aim To compare the associations and discriminatory performance of the fibrosis-4 index (FIB-4), atherogenic index of plasma (AIP), and triglyceride-glucose (TyG) index for all-cause mortality (ACM) and cardiovascular mortality (CVDM) in adults with FLI-defined MASLD. Methods This prospective cohort analysis included 4,037 adults with FLI-defined MASLD from NHANES 2011–2018. Mortality was ascertained through linkage to the National Death Index through December 31, 2019. Survey-weighted Cox models, restricted cubic splines, and 5-year time-dependent ROC analyses were used to evaluate associations and discrimination. Age-stratified analyses were performed because age is a component of FIB-4. Results During a median follow-up of approximately 4.5 years, 222 all-cause deaths and 66 cardiovascular deaths occurred. In fully adjusted age-stratified models, each 1-SD increase in FIB-4 was associated with higher ACM risk in participants aged < 65 years (HR 1.24, 95% CI 1.09–1.41) and ≥ 65 years (HR 1.34, 95% CI 1.20–1.50). FIB-4 was also associated with CVDM among participants aged ≥ 65 years (HR 1.37, 95% CI 1.19–1.59), whereas AIP and TyG were not significantly associated with CVDM in this age stratum. As standalone markers, FIB-4 showed higher 5-year discrimination than AIP and TyG for ACM (AUC 0.763 vs. 0.494 and 0.522) and CVDM (AUC 0.785 vs. 0.505 and 0.557). In sensitivity analyses using US-FLI-defined MASLD, the association of FIB-4 with ACM remained significant, and additional adjustment for lipid- and glucose-lowering medications did not materially alter the primary estimates. Conclusions In adults with FLI-defined MASLD, FIB-4 showed stronger near-term mortality risk stratification than AIP and TyG as standalone markers. The cardiovascular findings should be interpreted cautiously given the limited number of events and their sensitivity to the operational MASLD definition.

Functional and Density-Driven Errors in Density Functional Theory: Quantum Monte Carlo Benchmarks for Solids
abstractText: Abstract We introduce a systematic analysis of density functional approximation errors in solids by separating functional-driven from density-driven contributions using quantum Monte Carlo densities of silicon, sodium chloride, and copper as reference. Typically, functional errors dominate, but we identify important exceptions where the xc component of the density-driven error exceeds the functional error, notably for SOGGA11 in the semiconductor and the insulator. Material dependence is striking: 61% of functionals show error cancellation in silicon versus 16% in copper, and only five functionals surpass LDA accuracy for metallic copper even with exact densities. For silicon and sodium chloride, GILL or BECKE exchange combined with PBE, PW91, or P86 correlation achieves near-exact xc energies on QMC densities, while copper requires specialized functionals like PBEsol or PBELYP. High-quality densities consistently reduce density-driven errors across all systems. Historical analysis reveals that 1990s GGA functionals outperform many modern meta-GGAs, contradicting expectations of systematic improvement along Jacob’s ladder. These results provide practical guidance for functional selection and highlight implications for machine learning potential development, where material-dependent error cancellation may compromise transferability.

title: Graph‐Based Automated Discovery of Concise Soil Hydraulic Functions From Data: Beyond Empirical Formulations
abstractText: Abstract Soil hydraulic functions underpin water flow and transport modeling in the vadose zone, yet they are commonly represented by expert‐designed formulations such as the Mualem–van Genuchten (MvG) model. Because these formulations rest on predefined functional assumptions, balancing predictive accuracy and parametric compactness across soil textures remains challenging. Here we introduce a graph‐based equation discovery framework that distills soil hydraulic functions from experimental data. Reapplied to the original data sets that motivated the MvG parameterization, the framework recovers a concise water retention function together with an analytical unsaturated hydraulic conductivity expression whose mathematical structure departs from classical empirical forms. Evaluated across soils of contrasting texture, the discovered model predicts unsaturated hydraulic conductivity more accurately than MvG and its common variants, while its fitted parameters retain interpretable correlations with measurable soil physical properties. These findings suggest that data‐driven discovery can yield compact, analytically tractable constitutive relations that move beyond fixed empirical formulations.

title: Palliative care knowledge, opioid-related misconceptions, ethical attitudes, and perceptions of a good death among healthcare workers at a District General Hospital in Northern Sri Lanka: a cross-sectional study
abstractText: Despite growing recognition that access to palliative care and essential medicines for pain relief contributes to the realisation of the right to the highest attainable standard of health, as affirmed by World Health Assembly Resolution WHA67.19 (2014), healthcare workers in low-resource settings continue to face institutional, educational, and attitudinal barriers to its delivery. In Northern Sri Lanka, where the burden of serious illness is substantial and palliative care infrastructure remains underdeveloped, the knowledge, attitudes, and values of the clinical workforce have not previously been examined. This study assessed palliative care knowledge, opioid-related misconceptions, ethical attitudes toward end-of-life decision-making, and perceptions of a good death among healthcare workers at District General Hospital (DGH) Vavuniya. A cross-sectional survey was conducted between February and April 2024 among healthcare workers at DGH Vavuniya, Northern Province, Sri Lanka. A total of 200 questionnaires were distributed by stratified random sampling across professional categories: medical officers, nursing officers, paramedical staff, and administrative staff. A self-administered, multi-domain instrument assessed five domains: palliative care knowledge (seven scored items), opioid-related attitudes (three opioid-related belief/attitude items and two scenario-based belief and clinical judgement items), ethical attitudes and end-of-life decision-making (two items and one hypothetical vignette), good death perceptions (seven items), and demographics. Descriptive statistics and chi-square analyses were performed using SPSS version 26.0. The response rate was 84.0% ( n = 168/200). Of the 168 respondents, 60.1% ( n = 101) demonstrated adequate palliative care knowledge (score ≥ 5/7). A large majority, 91.1% ( n = 153), expressed a desire to receive further training in palliative care. Opioid-related misconceptions were prevalent: 58.3% ( n = 98) believed that therapeutic opioid use leads to addiction, and 41.1% ( n = 69) expressed concern about respiratory depression with standard analgesic doses. These misconceptions were distributed across professional categories without significant variation by years of clinical experience. Most respondents, 79.2% ( n = 133), supported withholding disproportionate interventions in patients with no realistic prospect of recovery, and 72.6% ( n = 122) endorsed prognostic disclosure as an ethical obligation. Regarding pain relief, 97.0% ( n = 163) agreed that every patient should have access to adequate pain relief, consistent with the aspirations expressed in World Health Assembly Resolution WHA67.19 (2014). A strong majority, 88.1% ( n = 148), identified freedom from pain as the most essential element of a good death, and 84.5% ( n = 142) preferred dying in the company of family. Healthcare workers at DGH Vavuniya demonstrated strong expressed support for palliative care principles alongside significant gaps in pharmacological knowledge and persistent opioid-related misconceptions. The prevalence of these misconceptions did not differ significantly by years of clinical experience. Prospective studies are needed to determine whether targeted educational interventions can modify these beliefs in this setting.

title: Deep learning identification of SST teleconnections driving early-winter North Atlantic climate
abstractText: Seasonal predictability over the North Atlantic-European (NAE) sector is strongly modulated by the background climate state, particularly in early winter. In this season, different El Niño-Southern Oscillation (ENSO) teleconnections have been reported before and after the 1990s. However, these studies rely on linear analysis, and the reasons for this lack of stationarity and its implications for seasonal forecasting have not yet been fully assessed. Here, we evaluate the non-stationarity of early-winter ENSO teleconnections over the NAE using a non-linear framework, the Neural Network forecast application (NN4CAST). The NN4CAST model predicts November-December mean sea-level pressure anomalies from October sea surface temperature (SST) anomalies. The neural network achieves skill comparable to the ECMWF seasonal forecasting system (SEAS5), and even exceeds it in certain regions like the NAE, despite relying only on October SST predictors. The model skilfully predicts the dominant NAE atmospheric variability modes, with a predictability that is strongly period-dependent. In particular, significant skill is found over the North Atlantic Oscillation centres of action during 1970–1995, especially for the Iceland region, whereas for the East Atlantic pattern, the improvement comes in recent decades (1996–2019). This teleconnection shift is mainly associated with Pacific SST anomalies, with recent decades marked by an intensified Southeast Asian Rossby wave source and a southward displacement of the North Atlantic jet stream. Our results demonstrate that explainable artificial intelligence can identify state-dependent SST precursors of NAE predictability, bridging data-driven and mechanistic understanding of climate teleconnections.

title: Genetic diversity and core SNP marker development for dragon fruit (Selenicereus spp.) germplasm identification and breeding
abstractText: Abstract Dragon fruit ( Selenicereus spp. ) is a nutritious and economically important tropical and subtropical fruit crop, mainly cultivated in Central America, Southeast Asia and East Asia. However, the molecular basis of flesh color variation remains poorly understood. Traditional germplasm classification mainly relies on phenotypic traits such as fruit skin and flesh color and stem morphology, which often leads to misclassification due to phenotypic similarity and frequent interspecific hybridization, thus hindering efficient breeding and germplasm utilization. In this study, we used SLAF-seq to develop SNP markers and perform genetic characterization on 45 dragon fruit accessions, and obtained 1,206,498 high-quality SNPs after strict filtering. Genetic diversity analysis showed that the diversity levels of the three main taxa were significantly higher than the overall level. Population structure and phylogenetic analyses clearly distinguished three genetic groups and corrected several misclassified accessions. Furthermore, we constructed a hierarchical core SNP marker set, among which the 10-SNP ultra-core panel showed optimal discrimination ability with 100% accuracy in independent germplasm validation. This panel effectively overcame the misleading effect of flesh color phenotype caused by hybrid germplasm. This study clarified the genetic diversity and population structure of cultivated dragon fruit, resolved germplasm classification confusion, and developed a set of efficient and diagnostic SNP markers. Furthermore, through phenotype-driven SNP screening and transcriptomic analysis, we identified four candidate genes (bHLH, CYP450, POD12, and MATE transporter) that show strong co-expression with key betalain biosynthesis genes ( CYP76AD1-1 and DODA1 ), providing molecular insights into flesh color regulation. These results provide a solid foundation for germplasm management, parental selection and molecular-assisted breeding of dragon fruit, and will promote the genetic improvement and sustainable development of this important horticultural crop.

title: Policy, Stigma, and the Haven of Safety: A Comparative Review of Global Baby Box Practices and the Sociocultural Context for Anonymous Infant Relinquishment in the United States
abstractText: Abstract Purpose of Review This narrative review aims to examine global “baby box” practices and compare them with United States Safe Haven Laws (SHL) and emerging baby box policies. The examination seeks to analyze how different nations incorporate these practices within their healthcare systems and evaluate contemporary infant relinquishment across diverse sociocultural contexts. Recent Findings Global analysis indicates that baby hatches function as a “last resort” in nations with high social stigma towards unwed and teenage mothers, or those with restrictive reproductive laws, such as Poland, where they serve as religious symbols of mercy. In the U.S., while SHL are universal, they lack uniformity in age limits, ranging from 3 to 90 days. Recent data show no significant correlation between legislated age limits and neonaticide rates, and some studies reveal that many healthcare providers feel unprepared or are unaware of these laws. Furthermore, baby boxes in the U.S. may be underutilized or misused, as seen in Texas and South Carolina where many surrenders still occur outside of legal frameworks. Summary While SHL provide critical alternatives to unsafe abandonment, they are insufficient as standalone solutions because they do not address root causes such as poverty, lack of support, and maternal mental health crises. Future research and clinical interventions must expand beyond preventing neonaticide to prioritize prenatal care, postpartum screening, and reducing the stigma of unwanted pregnancy. Promoting “open” or “confidential” hospital births is recommended to ensure both neonatal safety and maternal medical care, fostering a more holistic approach to reproductive health.

title: REGAIN : REconciliation GAIN ‐Driven Auxiliary Direction Learning
abstractText: ABSTRACT Forecast reconciliation usually starts from a fixed measurement system and asks how forecasts should be projected onto a coherent space. We ask a different question: which additional linear measurements should be forecasted and included in the reconciliation system? We propose REGAIN, a reconciliation‐gain framework that learns normalized auxiliary directions, forecasts the induced series with a frozen forecasting oracle, and selects auxiliary directions according to their reduction in weighted forecasting loss on the target variables after reconciliation. Unlike variance‐based components or predictability‐based auxiliary selection, REGAIN optimizes the downstream effect of an auxiliary measurement on the final reconciled forecasts. We provide a statistical characterization showing that useful auxiliary directions must provide additional information about target forecast errors beyond that contained in the original forecasts, rather than merely being easy to forecast. We further investigate the variance‐reduction effect of auxiliary augmentation, the role of forecast bias in overall prediction accuracy, and the impact of covariance estimation errors on this effect. A stagewise algorithm sequentially searches for auxiliary directions, screens them using held‐out forecast improvement, with an optional joint refinement step for the selected directions. Experiments on Beijing PM2.5 and Australian Tourism data show that gain‐selected measurements can improve both ordinary multivariate and hierarchical forecasts, especially when they reveal residual uncertainty not captured by the original measurement system.

title: Constraint internalization through parametric reconstruction: A legality-aware framework for geometric optimization problems
abstractText: Geometric optimization problems such as \(PA + k \cdot PB\) are commonly solved using reflection methods, projection techniques, or calculus-based optimization. In elementary treatments, these approaches often assume that signed algebraic expressions directly represent non-negative geometric distances across the entire real domain. When the variable extends beyond the traditional geometric boundary, this implicit assumption fails, creating what we describe as a representation legality gap. In this paper, we propose a parametric reconstruction framework that internalizes geometric admissibility constraints into the algebraic representation. Rather than partitioning the variable domain through piecewise case distinctions, we introduce an admissible auxiliary scaffold parameter \(L \ge x\) to decompose the objective function into a geometrically legal core path and an algebraically compensating residual. The auxiliary parameter \(L\) cancels identically in the reconstructed representation, ensuring global validity across \(\mathbb{R}\). We demonstrate this framework on a classical Hu Bugui-type optimization problem, establish the global minimum via dynamic projection inequalities, prove the exact invariance of the minimizer, and extend the result to an isomorphic parametric family.

title: Three advanced lectures on inflation
Carbon fluxes in rhodoliths, coraliths and artificial substrates on tropical reefs
abstractText: Abstract Understanding how calcifying benthic systems contribute to short-term carbon dynamics helps assess their role in shallow tropical ecosystems under environmental change. We compared day-to-night relative patterns of net organic carbon production and net calcification in three contrasting functional units from the Colombian Caribbean: rhodoliths, spherical free-living colonies (coraliths) of the coral Siderastrea radians , and colonized artificial substrates mimicking the rhodolith shape. In situ incubations were conducted during morning, afternoon, and nighttime periods under natural environmental conditions. We observed significant variation among incubation periods and across all functional units, with higher daytime net organic carbon production and calcification and reduced or negative nighttime values. Rhodoliths exhibited the highest daytime rates of both net organic carbon production and net calcification and the greatest morning-to-night contrast in net calcification (11.6-fold). Colonized artificial substrates showed the greatest contrast in net organic carbon production (5.37-fold) and consistent nighttime net CaCO₃ dissolution, whereas corals exhibited comparatively lower daytime rates and more moderate contrasts. Morning-to-night metabolic ratios revealed marked differences among functional units in the relative magnitude of daytime net organic carbon production and the measured nighttime respiratory rate, as well as in the relative magnitude of light and dark calcification rates. Daytime net organic carbon production and light calcification showed contrasting relationships among systems. Corals exhibited proportionally higher net organic carbon production relative to calcification than rhodoliths and colonized artificial substrates. Calcifying benthic systems differ not only in metabolic magnitude but also in the temporal expression of organic and inorganic carbon processes. In addition, the artificial substrates provide a potentially scalable experimental platform for exploring short-term metabolic and carbonate dynamics associated with colonized structures in reef-associated environments. Biological organization and substrate identity influence fine-scale carbonate chemistry variability in shallow tropical ecosystems, with implications for understanding benthic carbon cycling and the ecological functioning of natural and artificial reef-associated habitats.

title: Serum trace element profiles and gallbladder cancer risk in an Indian population: evidence from a case–control study
abstractText: Gallbladder cancer (GBC), a rare yet aggressive biliary tract malignancy, exhibits marked geographic variation in incidence, with particularly high rates reported across northern and eastern India (including the gangetic plain) as well as parts of north-eastern India. This spatial distribution suggests that environmental exposures and region-specific risk factors play a significant role in GBC etiology. This study aimed to investigate the association of serum essential and non-essential trace elements, individually and as mixtures, with GBC risk. In this hospital-based case–control study, a total of 912 GBC cases and 1140 visitor controls were enrolled at Tata Memorial Hospital, India. The concentration of non-essential (Cr, Ni, As, Cd, Pb, U) and essential elements (Mn, Cu, Se) were measured in serum samples, following acid digestion with trace metal-grade nitric acid (50-fold dilution), using ICP-MS. With highly right-skewed distributions, trace element concentrations were log-transformed for statistical and sensitivity analysis. Individual effects were presented using logistic regression model adjusting for prespecified confounders, while joint metal mixture effects were obtained using WQS and qgcomp methods. In addition to primary logistic regression analysis, two-part and winsorization models were performed to assess the robustness of findings. A strong non-linear association for Cu, Mn, Cd and U (P-overall ≤ 0.05 ; P-nonlinear ≤ 0.05 ) was observed. The strongest inter-metal correlation was observed for Mn-U. Exposure to metal mixture showed one-unit increase in the WQS index with increased GBC risk (OR = 6.19; 95% CI 4.84–7.95; P ≤ 0.001 ), with the highest weight contributed by Cu (~ 60%), followed by Cd (~26 %) and Mn (~ 13%). A DAG-informed confounder set, applied to an internal validation dataset generated from the training-validation split, confirmed a significant WQS-GBC association (OR = 2.71; 95% CI 2.26–3.25; P ≤ 0.001 ), supporting the robustness of the primary metal mixture findings. An exploratory mediation analysis indicated no statistically significant evidence of mediation through gallstone (β ACME : 0.01; 95% CI − 0.00–0.03; P = 0.064). Metal mixtures might be significantly associated with GBC and identification of the source of exposure, particularly in the high-risk areas of the GBC, would be useful in primary prevention.

title: Dimming and pulsation shock of the coalesced star V838 Monocerotis
abstractText: V838 Monocerotis is the remnant of a stellar merger that occurred in 2002. Twenty-four years after the merger, the remnant closely resembles a red supergiant, but its luminosity is sustained by core hydrogen burning and continued contraction toward hydrostatic equilibrium. In late 2025, the system entered the deepest dimming event observed since 2006. We characterized the 2026 dimming event of V838 Mon using multiband photometry and high-resolution spectroscopy spanning from the dimming minimum through the recovery phase, and investigated whether the merger remnant exhibits pulsations analogous to those seen in red supergiants and Mira stars. We obtained UBVRI and JHK_s photometry with the NOT telescope and extracted light curves from the public AAVSO, ATLAS, ZTF, and ASAS-SN databases and services, covering the entire dimming event. These data were supplemented by time-series spectra acquired with SALT/HRS, LBT/PEPSI, VLT/X-shooter, and VLT/UVES, covering the spectral range 3760--24,800 Å at resolutions R=6,700--130,000. Differential spectra were constructed by comparison with pre-dimming spectra from 2024. The photometric color evolution during the dimming can be well reproduced by gray dust extinction with A_V = 1.3±0.1 mag. This is consistent with a transiting clump of freshly formed circumstellar dust. The photospheric effective temperature changed by no more than ≈200 K during the event. During the recovery phase, hydrogen recombination lines from Balmer, Paschen, and Brackett series appeared in emission. Their line ratios do not follow the Case B standard but are reminiscent of hydrogen emission in pulsating M-type Mira stars near maximum light. These features are interpreted as arising from a pulsation shock propagating outward from below the photosphere. Simultaneously, low-ionization metal lines appeared blueshifted by 90 ̨ms relative to the stellar rest frame, tracing shock-accelerated gas on the near side of the stellar disk. The spectroscopic sequence suggests that the 2026 dimming was itself triggered by a preceding pulsation shock that occurred earlier in 2025 when the star was in conjunction with the Sun. We present the first observational evidence for pulsations in a stellar merger remnant. Twenty-four years after the coalescence event, V838 Mon exhibits pulsation shocks closely resembling those seen in red supergiants and Mira stars, providing observational support for predicted pulsational instability in post-merger objects. The observed shock may trigger a subsequent dimming event later in 2026.

title: Crop Load Management of Plums Using 1-Aminocyclopropane Carboxylic Acid (1-ACC)
abstractText: Excessive fruit set in European (Prunus domestica L.) and Japanese (Prunus salicina L.) plum trees necessitates thinning to optimize crop load, enhance fruit quality, and reduce manual hand thinning. This study evaluated the efficacy of the ethylene precursor 1-aminocyclopropane-1-carboxylic acid (1-ACC) as a chemical thinning agent for the European plum cultivar ‘Vibrant’ and the Japanese plum cultivar ‘Early Golden’. Treatments were applied at full bloom (FB) and at the fruitlet stage (8-10 mm diameter) using 1-ACC concentrations of 150, 300, and 450 mg·L⁻¹. Horticultural measurements included crop load, yield, fruit size distribution, fruit quality, phytotoxic effects, and crop value. Applications of 1-ACC effectively reduced crop load, with FB applications producing greater thinning responses than fruitlet-stage applications. Increasing application rates resulted in decreased yield and crop value, while average fruit weight increased. No hand thinning was required in both years of the study due to poor pollination in the ‘Early Golden’ orchard and atypical fruit drop unrelated to 1-ACC treatments following early fruit development in the ‘Vibrant’ orchard; therefore, commercial thinning was not required. Thinning responses varied by cultivar and application timing, underscoring the importance of cultivar-specific thinning strategies. Ethylene evolution following 1-ACC application supported its role in fruit abscission, with ethylene peaks observed within 24 h and differing in intensity by application timing. These results indicate that 1-ACC is a viable chemical thinning agent for plums, although optimization of application timing and concentration, particularly in seasons with heavier fruit set, is required to balance thinning efficacy with economic returns.

title: Efficacy and safety of minocycline in acute ischaemic stroke by time of first dose and onset-to-treatment time: a secondary analysis of the EMPHASIS trial
abstractText: Background: Minocycline improved functional outcomes in EMPHASIS, but timing-related consistency is uncertain. We assessed treatment effects by first-dosing clock time and onset-to-first-dosing interval. Methods: EMPHASIS was a phase 3, multicentre, double-blind, randomised, placebo-controlled trial at 58 Chinese hospitals. Patients aged 18–80 years with acute ischaemic stroke within 72 h and NIHSS 4–25 were assigned 1:1 to oral minocycline or placebo. This prespecified subgroup analysis categorised first-dosing clock time as daytime, evening, or overnight, and onset-to-first-dosing interval as ≤24 h, >24–48 h, or >48 h. The primary outcome was 90-day mRS 0–1. Treatment-by-subgroup interactions were tested in adjusted models. Findings: Between May 19, 2023, and May 20, 2024, 1724 patients were assigned (862 per group). Minocycline increased 90-day mRS 0–1 versus placebo (447/850 [52·6%] vs 403/851 [47·4%]; absolute difference 5·2 percentage points, 95% CI 0·5–10·0; adjusted RR 1·14, 95% CI 1·03–1·25; P=0·012). No significant interaction was detected by first-dosing clock time (P for interaction=0·559) or onset-to-first-dosing interval (P for interaction=0·604). Symptomatic intracranial haemorrhage at 24 h occurred in one minocycline patient and none receiving placebo. Interpretation: We found no statistical evidence that minocycline effects differed by first-dosing clock time or onset-to-first-dosing interval within 72 h; these exploratory findings do not establish an optimal dosing time.

title: Alkyl Side-Chain and Ionic-Block Design of Mixed-Charge Polyurethane Copolymer Hydrogels: from Nanostructure and Viscoelasticity to Thermo-Optical and Mechanical Properties
abstractText: Abstract Mixed-charge polyurethane (MCPU) copolymers with tunable alkyl side chains (C1, C6, and C18) and ionic-block ratios (60% and 70%) were synthesized and assembled into single-network (SN) physical hydrogels. Three different nanostructures were identified by small-angle X-ray scattering: weakly segregated domains (C1), periodic microphase separation (C6), and microphase separation with interdigitated lamellar ordering (C18). Rheology studies provide a macroscopic relaxation timescale (τrelax) that quantifies the rate of noncovalent network rearrangement. The SN hydrogels with relatively short τrelax values (C1 and C6) exhibit thermo-optical switching, whereas C18 remains opaque. Blending the MCPU with a covalently crosslinked poly(2-hydroxyethyl methacrylate) network generates double-network hydrogels that preserve the thermo-optical switching performance. Monotonic tensile toughness peaks at the intermediate side chain (C6), whereas C18 maximizes the modulus, strength, and per-cycle energy dissipation. However, the cyclic durability test shows that C1 survives 50,000 cycles, and C18, which dissipates the most energy per cycle, fails after approximately 637 cycles. τrelax therefore tracks both the thermo-optical switchability and cyclic durability, providing a kinetic parameter that links them.

title: Effect of silicon carbide (SiC) nanomaterials on the performance of the disc brake pads in vehicles: an experimental study
abstractText: Abstract Composite materials are used in many industries, and one of the most important industries in which composite materials are used is the automobile industry. One of the parts whose performance depends most on composite materials in vehicles is the brake pads. The wear rate, friction rate, cooling rate, and overall brake performance depend on it. This study investigates the enhancement of brake pad performance by incorporating silicon carbide (SiC) nanoparticles as an abrasive additive. Testing was conducted on a specialized rig utilizing a standard grey cast iron ventilated disc (outer diameter of 241 mm and nominal thickness of 19 mm), consistent with the specifications of a 2005 Hyundai Excel. Four experimental formulations with SiC concentrations of 0, 0.5, 1.5, and 3 wt% were evaluated. The results demonstrate that the 0.5 wt% SiC concentration achieved the most significant improvement, increasing the average brake force by up to 19% and enhancing the friction coefficient compared to unmodified pads. Furthermore, the SiC-infused samples exhibited superior thermal stability and fade resistance at temperatures up to 130 °C, outperforming all other tested formulations and demonstrating more consistent reliability under different operating conditions.

title: SPARC is involved in the transition from DCIS to invasive ductal carcinoma via a TGFBR-dependent mechanism in breast cancer
abstractText: Ductal carcinoma in situ (DCIS) presents a variable risk of progression to invasive ductal carcinoma (IDC), yet reliable predictors of this transition are limited. Membrane type I matrix metalloproteinase (MT1-MMP) is a key regulator of this progression. We combined RNA sequencing of MT1-MMPhigh and MT1-MMPlow cell populations from intraductal tumor xenografts with human high-grade DCIS datasets to identify regulators of early breast cancer progression. Data from 1100 breast cancer patients in The Cancer Genome Atlas (TCGA) were analyzed (Pearson's correlation). Protein expressions were analyzed by IHC on three independent human cohorts (n = 231, Friedman test). siRNA-mediated knockdown of Secreted Protein Acidic and Cysteine Rich (SPARC) and pharmacological inhibition of TGF-β receptor type I (TGFBR), gelatin degradation and cell migration assays were employed to analyze the role of the TGFBRI–SPARC–MT1-MMP axis in breast cancer invasion (ANOVA). A new intraductal syngeneic mice model was used for testing TGFBRI inhibitors in the DCIS-to-IDC transition (ANOVA). SPARC was identified as an invasive switch candidate, upregulated in DCIS versus normal epithelium, further increased in IDC, and correlated with MT1-MMP expression. Functionally, SPARC depletion reduced MT1-MMP, matrix degradation, and TGF-β signaling. TGFBRI inhibition decreased SPARC and MT1-MMP levels, matrix degradation, cell migration, and DCIS-to-IDC transition in a triple-negative intraductal syngeneic mouse model. Notably, SPARC did not associate with metastasis, confirming its specific role in early progression. Our findings highlight the TGFBRI–SPARC–MT1-MMP axis as a promising therapeutic target for preventing early breast cancer invasion.

title: Beyond the Exchange Picture of Singlet–Triplet Gaps
abstractText: Abstract Molecules with inverted singlet–triplet gaps are promising candidates for next-generation organic light-emitting diode emitters, but identifying general principles that explain and guide singlet–triplet inversion remains challenging. Here, we investigate substituted heptazines, vibrational ensembles of azupyrene and isopyrene, and a chemically diverse molecular set using CIS, EOM-CCSD, and wave function-based state matching. The CIS analysis reveals an intermediate level of electronic response between direct exchange and correlation: state-specific configuration relaxation redistributes the gap among exchange, orbital-energy, and electron–hole Coulomb contributions. Correlation beyond CIS generally lowers the gap, with a larger reduction associated with greater relative double-excitation character in the singlet. However, the final gap also depends on the positive CIS baseline, so similar doubles content can occur in systems with either positive or negative gaps. Within related molecular data sets, a larger CIS baseline is accompanied by a stronger correlation-driven reduction, but this relationship does not hold across chemically diverse molecules. These findings establish the importance of balancing the full state-specific singles baseline against correlation-driven gap reduction when interpreting and designing singlet–triplet energetics.

title: Handling of the Non-Assessable Verbal Glasgow Coma Scale and Computed Illness Severity in Critically Ill Adults with Acute Brain Injury: A Retrospective Analysis
abstractText: Background The Glasgow Coma Scale (GCS) contributes to illness-severity scores. The verbal component cannot be observed in intubated patients; the MIMIC Code Repository sets “No Response-ETT” rows to a total of 15. Objective To quantify non-assessable verbal GCS examinations and describe how their handling changes computed severity, the analyzed population and mortality-model performance. Materials and Methods Retrospective MIMIC-IV cohort (Boston, 2008 to 2022) of adults with acute brain injury (first intensive care unit stay per hospitalization); a “No Response-ETT” verbal entry was non-assessable. Five GCS derivation strategies were compared; four used the lowest eye-plus-motor examination of the first 24 h. The eICU Collaborative Research Database (eICU-CRD; United States, 2014 to 2015) supported replication. Results Of 14,230 stays, 45.2% had a non-assessable verbal examination; 47.5% of ventilated stays had none assessable in the first 24 h. A non-assessable lowest examination was associated with mechanical ventilation (adjusted odds ratio, 32.8; 95% CI, 27.8 to 38.6). The official first-day GCS was 15 in 44.7% of 14 215 stays; 94.1% of default-rule totals of 15 were incompatible with the eye-plus-motor sum charted at that examination. With one mortality-model specification refitted per GCS derivation on the same stays, the area under the receiver operating characteristic curve was 0.749 (95% CI, 0.739 to 0.760) with the official first-day GCS and 0.820 (0.812 to 0.828) with an eye-and-motor (Brennan) estimate. Complete-case analysis excluded 5509 of 14 192 stays and 72.8% of deaths. In eICU-CRD, stays with an unscored GCS component had higher mortality (16.6% vs 9.2%), but totals of 12 or more were no more frequent after the first documented ventilation entry (17.3%) than before (19.5%). Conclusion In this cohort, how a non-assessable verbal GCS was handled changed computed severity and the analyzed population. Studies and benchmarks that use GCS-based severity should report the handling rule.

title: Self-propelled aquatic locomotion by an elastically mounted flexible foil actuated by an oscillating force
abstractText: An analytical formulation of the fluid-structure interaction of a flexible foil driven by an oscillating force actuating on its elastically mounted leading edge is used to investigate self-propelled aquatic locomotion of a virtual body (modelled by just a constant drag coefficient) via the flexible foil, which can heave, pitch and deform passively with the hydrodynamic forces. The small-amplitude theoretical model is compared and validated with previous theoretical and experimental results for a body propelled by a rigid plate oscillating with a prescribed heaving motion and passive pitch. The inclusion of passive heave and deformation allows for expanding the parametric ranges for optimal self-propulsion conditions in terms of length travelled by flapping cycle (stride length) and locomotion efficiency. In addition to the known optimal locomotion condition localized near the resonance of the torsional spring on which the foil is elastically mounted, which here is modulated by its coupling with the resonances of the translational spring and of the structural deformation of the foil, another even better local optimal locomotion condition is found near the translational spring branch of the elastic support resonance that occurs at lower stiffnesses of both springs. Unlike the local maximum of the stride length close to the natural frequency associated with the torsional spring branch, which increases with the stiffness of the foil, being the highest for a rigid foil, the larger local maximum associated with the translational spring branch increases as the stiffness of the foil decreases, decreasing also the cost of transport.

title: When the grid overflows: a novel probabilistic framework to assess the success of storing excess electricity as heat in high-temperature ATES (HT-ATES) systems
abstractText: Abstract Increasing shares of variable renewable electricity (VRE) are creating more frequent periods of surplus electricity, increasing the need for flexible options that can absorb and use this excess generation. One option is to convert surplus electricity into heat, but its effective use requires storage when heat production and demand do not coincide. Because heat demand remains concentrated in the colder months, long-duration seasonal thermal storage is needed to bridge this temporal gap. High-temperature aquifer thermal energy storage (HT-ATES) is one technology capable of providing this seasonal storage function. This study develops a demand-oriented operational probability of success (PoS) framework for evaluating whether HT-ATES can convert historically observed surplus electricity into useful seasonal heat. The Neubrandenburg system in Germany was used as a physically grounded reference case. Historical German electricity data from 2015 to 2022 were represented through empirical four-week surplus distributions and coupled to a chronological Monte Carlo inventory model accounting for charging availability, well thermal throughput, adopted storage limit, and thermal recovery. The model first generated a distribution of achievable seasonal heat delivery, which was then evaluated against alternative heat-demand targets. PoS is therefore expressed as the probability that delivered heat meets or exceeds a specified thermal requirement, rather than as a fixed property of the aquifer. For the base configuration, with a thermal power of approximately 3.72 MW, an adopted storage limit of 12 GWh, and a recovery factor of 0.72, the 20,000 retained Monte Carlo cycles produced a mean seasonal delivery of 8.551 GWh. The upper modeled heat delivery of 8.640 GWh was reached in 94.63% of the cycles. Constraint diagnostics showed that well throughput was the unique limiting condition in 57.06% of injection decisions, remaining storage space in 28.82%, and zero-surplus charging windows in 10.90%, while positive-surplus magnitude alone did not limit any base-case injection decision. Sensitivity analyses further showed that increasing thermal power shifts the range of heat-demand targets that can be met with high probability, but the benefit diminishes as the modeled upper delivery limit is approached. Equivalent non-interacting doublet configurations exhibit the same throughput-storage-limit trade-off. The results demonstrate that nominal storage capacity alone is insufficient for assessing HT-ATES performance. Operational success depends jointly on charging opportunities, thermal power, storage capacity, thermal recovery, system configuration, and the thermal target used to define success. The proposed framework provides a transferable screening method for linking historical energy-system variability with subsurface storage constraints and explicit heat-delivery requirements.

title: Plastic matters: it drives soil aggregation, carbon retention, nutrient cycling, and microbial communities dependent on its degradability
abstractText: Microplastics (MPs) have shown different effects on soil physical structure, chemistry, and microbial communities. As soils are known to differ in their potential to develop structure, the observed variability in MP effects may be strongly attributed to MPs impact on soil aggregation. Hence, we here address the impact of different MPs on soil aggregation and associated soil functions such as water, carbon, and nutrient storage, and microbial habitat in soils differing in texture and soil organic matter (SOM). We hypothesized that conventional MPs hinder soil aggregation, speeding up the turnover of soil inherent OM, and reducing soil water holding capacity (WHC), while degradable MPs represent substrates altering soil microbial community composition, and directly promoting microbial activity and nutrient turnover. To address this, Zea mays was planted in a greenhouse with silty loam and sandy loam soil and spiked with polyethylene (PE), polyethylene terephthalate (PET), or biodegradable polybutylene adipate terephthalate (PBAT), varied by concentration (0%, 0.1%, 1% w/w) and size (200–400, 75–200, <75 µm). Soil aggregate fractions and stability, WHC, 15 N-ammonium-nitrate and 13 C-yeast as models for soil N and C cycling, available P and K, as well as plant growth, and microbiota within aggregate fractions were analyzed. Overall, MP addition led to a decrease in more stable, occluded soil microaggregates, and a respective increase in free aggregates, while macroaggregate fractions remained unaffected. For both soils and across all MPs, soil C retention was reduced about 50%. Soil texture dominated the response of soil to MP addition: finer-textured soils lost more microaggregates, around 25% greater SOM turnover, and 33% lower WHC. As this was independent of polymer size and type, we relate this to physical MP effects. An MP-specific biochemical effect was observed for biodegradable PBAT tending to increase soil microaggregate formation, stability, and WHC. It led to 15 N immobilization in soil and increased plant uptake and significantly altered soil prokaryotic communities in aggregate fractions. Here, microbial taxa involved in reductive nitrogen cycling, depletion of N-fixing Azospirillum spp., and enrichment of the potentially plant-pathogenic Xylophilus spp. was observed. We reveal that MPs exert fundamentally bidirectional effects on soils. Biodegradable MPs enhance beneficial properties such as aggregation and water retention yet concurrently disrupt key microbiome functions. Across all polymer types, MPs accelerate soil C turnover, underscoring the need to resolve their net impact on critical soil functions in a soil- and polymer-specific context.

title: Process design and enhancement of extraction distillation for separating n-propanol and dimethyl carbonate using imidazolium-based ionic liquids
abstractText: Abstract Extractive distillation (ED) ranks among the most potent methods when it comes to resolving azeotropic separation challenges, and the performance of the extractant is the core factor affecting process efficiency. This study centers on the challenges associated with the separation of the DMC-NPA azeotropic mixture. Initially, by virtue of COSMO theory and quantum chemical principles, [EMim][AC] was identified as the optimal extractant from a pool of 40 imidazolium-based ionic liquids (ILs). Then, molecular dynamics simulation techniques were employed to unravel the intrinsic extraction mechanism of the extractant. Finally, the separation design was simulated via Aspen V14 with [EMim][AC] as the extractant, and the results of multi-objective optimization (MOO) showed the [EMim][AC]-ED system demonstrates inferior TAC and diminished gas emissions when contrasted with the DMSO-HIED process. In addition, heat integration was performed on the [EMim][AC]-ED process, reducing the TAC to 1.1032 $/Y and Gas emissions to 1420.30 kg/Y, with reductions of 1.77% and 4.58% respectively, proving that [EMim][AC]-HIED was more valuable for application.

Modeling associations between migratory movements and seasonal honey bee colony survival: a machine-learning approach with big data
abstractText: Abstract This study investigates the impact of commercial beekeeping practices, specifically colony movement and co-variates, on honeybee colony survival. We used data on 362,884 colonies from 62 beekeepers over 4 years (2022-2026) to compare the numberof times a given hive was moved to the survival or death of those hives. We found that excessive transportation significantlyreduces the probability of surviving beyond one season. We also found a positive effect between the predicted longevity andthe average days between moves, suggesting movement strategy could mitigate the negative impact of movements on longevity.Finally, we’ve compared 3 machine learning survival models and their combination on C-index and Brier score. We’ve thenselected the best model and data format for the features importance and simulation. We generated 15 different movementsscenarios on 3 simulated beekeeping seasons. The results of our model comparison highlight the importance of a proper datastructure to achieve optimal performance on censored data.

title: Novel paper-based electrochemical system for detection of anti-spike protein antibodies from SARS-CoV-2
abstractText: Abstract A novel disposable paper-based electrochemical biosensor for detecting anti-spike protein antibodies is presented, featuring the innovative use of carbon dots derived from a biological source and a liposome–biorecognition element complex. The optimized electrochemical sensing platform is described and characterized, regarding its structural and functional properties. The sensor showed a linear response between 0.0010 and 10 µg mL − 1 , demonstrating high sensitivity and a low limit of detection (LOD) of 1.78 pg mL − 1 , as well as good selectivity. Real nasopharyngeal swab samples were tested for the first time using this type of paper-based electrochemical system for anti-spike antibody detection. This approach was designed to mimic the virus's response while ensuring greater sensitivity and selectivity. Overall, a new electrochemical method for screening anti-spike antibodies was developed to monitor vulnerable populations for new SARS-CoV-2 infections and track the development of adaptive immunity within communities, contributing to the development of future point-of-care (POC) analysis without the need for specialized personnel or laboratory facilities.

title: Design and calibration of a division-of-pupil snapshot polarization imaging system
Political stance detection on X during the 2024 U.S. election: a comparative study of classical, neural, and transformer models
abstractText: Abstract As online social networks (OSNs) play an increasingly influential role in political communication, accurately detecting political stance from noisy, short-form content remains a significant challenge in computational social science (CSS). This paper presents a controlled comparison of text classification models for political stance detection during the 2024 U.S. presidential election, focusing on candidate affiliation toward Donald Trump and Joe Biden–Kamala Harris. Using nearly 100,000 posts from X, we define candidate affiliation as a three-class target variable (Trump, Biden–Kamala, or Neutral) and use topic modeling to support keyword development and thematic characterization. Under a unified preprocessing, labeling, and evaluation pipeline, we compare classical machine learning models, sentence-embedding-based neural architectures, and a domain-adapted transformer. Results suggest that task-aligned text representation accounts for most of the predictive signal in this setting. While fine-tuned BERTweet achieves the strongest in-domain performance, carefully engineered classical models, particularly linear support vector machines, remain highly competitive. Multi-feature and ablation analyses further indicate that expanded metadata did not yield reliable gains beyond strong text representations. Overall, this work provides a controlled comparison of text models for candidate affiliation on a heuristically labeled corpus.

title: Structured robust control for a hybrid functional electrical stimulation exoskeleton system with uncertain dynamics
Green tea extract is associated with gut microbiota, immune, and tumor-marker changes in colorectal cancer models
abstractText: Colorectal cancer (CRC) is associated with mucosal inflammation, immune dysregulation, and gut microbiota imbalance. This study evaluated the biological effects of whole green tea extract (GTE) using EGCG-focused network pharmacology, a syngeneic CT26 tumor model, and an AOM/DSS-induced colitis-associated CRC model. Oral GTE was related to a lower tumor burden, attenuated systemic wasting, and preserved intestinal mucosal architecture. Fecal microbiota and metabolite analyses showed GTE-associated changes in microbial composition, enrichment of selected SCFA-associated taxa, including Bacteroides and Parabacteroides, and increased fecal short-chain fatty acids. These changes were accompanied by lower circulating IL-1β, IL-6, and TNF-α, reduced neutrophil-associated inflammatory indices, and increased splenic CD8+ T-cell populations. Tumor analyses showed reduced VEGF and Bcl-2 and increased Bax expression. EGCG-associated targets were enriched in cancer-, inflammation-, apoptosis-, and VEGF-related pathways. These findings suggest that whole GTE is associated with parallel changes in host inflammatory and immune indices, fecal microbiota/SCFA profiles, and tumor-related outcomes.

title: PPanGGOLiN V2: technical enhancement and extended functionalities for prokaryotic pangenome analysis
abstractText: The exponential growth of genomic data, particularly for microbes, has made pangenomic approaches a gold standard for large-scale comparative genomics. By capturing the full genomic diversity of a species rather than relying on a single reference, pangenomics has transformed microbial genomics, revealing the adaptive potential of bacteria and the evolutionary dynamics underlying functional diversity. Among available tools, PPanGGOLiN distinguishes itself through its graph-based model coupled with statistical gene partitioning. Here we present PPanGGOLiN v2, which introduces substantial improvements across three dimensions: new analytical features that expand what users can investigate, a comprehensive software architecture redesign that improves maintainability and extensibility, and performance improvements that address the computational demands of ever-growing genomic datasets.

title: Natural and anthropogenic factors associated with agricultural productivity in selected Sub-Saharan African countries: The role of water resources
abstractText: This study examines the impact of selected natural and anthropogenic factors on agricultural productivity in 19 Sub-Saharan African countries over the period 1990–2020, using panel data from the FAOSTAT database. Agricultural productivity is measured as kilocalories produced per hectare of agricultural land. The explanatory variables include fertilizer use, agricultural water withdrawal, water stress, population, and agricultural land per capita. The Hausman test supports a fixed-effects specification, which is therefore used in the analysis. The results indicate that population has a positive and statistically significant effect on agricultural productivity, while agricultural land per capita is negatively associated with productivity. Fertilizer use and agricultural water withdrawal are not statistically significant, while water stress shows a positive association with agricultural productivity. The findings suggest that the interaction of demographic pressure, land availability, and water-related constraints shapes agricultural productivity in selected Sub-Saharan African countries. The study highlights the need for improved water resource management, efficient land use, and sustainable agricultural intensification, alongside better-targeted use of production inputs, to support sustainable productivity growth and strengthen food security in Sub-Saharan Africa.

title: Two decades of sedimentation and contemporary urban contamination in Brazilian tropical coastal reefs
abstractText: In the face of ongoing climate changes, local mitigation strategies are key to strengthening the resilience of reef ecosystems. However, the lack of long-term, high-resolution environmental data limits our understanding of temporal changes and their effects on current reef conditions. Here, we applied an integrative monitoring approach in a shallow reef complex in northeastern Brazil, incorporating historical sedimentation rates, land-use changes, organic matter characterization, and sewage tracers (i.e., linear alkylbenzenes) across three distinct sampling sites. High sedimentation rates, associated with intensive agricultural land use in the region, indicate chronic environmental pressure, with spatial variation primarily driven by sediment resuspension. Organic matter (OM) associated with sewage inputs and linear alkylbenzene concentrations showed marked seasonal variability, with elevated levels during the dry season and periods of intensified tourism. In addition, a fine-scale spatial gradient was observed, with contamination concentrations decreasing with increasing distance from the fluvial source. The contribution of marine-derived OM was predominant throughout the year, while the input of continental material increased during the rainy season in a relatively homogeneous manner across sampled sites. These findings highlight chronic environmental stress in the coastal coral reef system, where accumulating stressors may further compromise coral resilience and benthic composition.

title: What Drives Negative K DP Above the Melting Layer? The Hidden Role of Secondary Ice Production
abstractText: Abstract Secondary ice production (SIP) remains a major uncertainty in understanding deep convection because its rates and controlling conditions are poorly constrained. Using the Tracking Aerosol Convection Interactions Experiment (TRACER) C‐band and operational S‐band radar observations, Houston Lightning Mapping Array (HLMA) lightning data, and large‐eddy simulations (LESs), this study investigates negative observed above the melting layer as a potential signature of SIP and storm electrification. Among 413 observed deep convective cells, 238 cases (∼57.6%) exhibit negative above the melting layer, and 49 of 123 lightning‐active cases (∼39.8%) show negative near HLMA sources. These observations suggest that negative is associated with small, vertically oriented, electrically aligned ice particles. LESs with spectral bin microphysics reproduce negative with high likelihood only when SIP is included, especially fragmentation of freezing drops, which increases ice water path, decreases liquid water path, and reduces accumulated precipitation by ∼11.2% in the examined case.

title: Antimicrobial cetylpyridinium chloride disrupts the mitochondrial electron transport chain with potency comparable to cyanide, via cardiolipin interference at cytochrome c
abstractText: Abstract People are widely exposed to the antimicrobial cetylpyridinium chloride (CPC) via consumer products, but CPC is a mitochondrial toxicant with potency comparable to that of canonical mitotoxicants. CPC is largely unregulated despite growing usage, bioavailability, and ability to cross the blood-brain barrier. Previously, we showed, in several cell types at non-cytotoxic and exposure-relevant doses, CPC inhibits ATP and oxygen consumption rate. Mitochondrial toxicity is linked to multiple diseases, but CPC has not been studied epidemiologically, and its mode of action is unknown. To determine why oxygen consumption is hampered by CPC, we hypothesized that CPC inhibits electron transport chain components, cardiolipin, or Krebs cycle enzymes. Here, we show that, in primary human skin cells, an immune mast cell model, and isolated mitochondria, CPC apparently inhibits multiple electron transport chain Complexes. Detailed investigation pinpointed the mechanism to the distal end of electron transport chain: Complex III-cytochrome c-Complex IV. Using multiple approaches, we show that CPC does not directly inhibit any of the Complexes, nor Krebs enzymes, nor coenzyme Q. Yet, CPC exhibits mitotoxicity with potency comparable to cyanide. In healthy mitochondria, the lipid cardiolipin attracts cytochrome c so that it may shuttle electrons from Complex III to IV. We present evidence implicating electrostatic CPC interference in cardiolipin-cytochrome c interactions. To provide data for focusing epidemiological investigations, clarifying risk analysis, and positing new mechanisms of action for predictive toxicology, we determined the biochemical mechanism of action of this ubiquitous chemical, a model for the large class of quaternary ammonium compounds.

title: Multifunctional Bioactive Compounds from Medicinal Plants: Antioxidant, Antimicrobial and Corrosion Inhibition Perspectives
abstractText: Abstract Medicinal plants are valuable sources of phenolics, flavonoids, alkaloids, terpenoids, glycosides and essential oils. Phytochemicals extracted from medicinal plants find application in different biological systems due to their varied biological activities. Rising environmental concerns along with requirement for sustainable substitutes have gained interest in multifunctional compounds from plants. Plants possess phytochemicals with antioxidant, antimicrobial and corrosion inhibition potential which make them applicable in pharmaceutical industries, food processing, environmental and industrial applications. Antioxidant potential involves free radical scavenging activity, metal chelating ability and regulation of redox reaction. Antimicrobial activity is due to alteration of the microbial cell membrane structure, enzyme inhibition and binding with microbial DNA. Corrosion inhibition potentials involve adsorption of bioactive compounds present in plants on metal surface and forming a protective layer over metal surface that reduces metal dissolution in acidic corrosive media. The multifunctional nature of these compounds is associated with the presence of aromatic rings and electron rich functional groups such as hydroxyl, carbonyl, and heteroatom containing groups. Compared with synthetic chemicals, plant-based compounds are biodegradable, eco-friendly and less toxic. Advances in extraction, characterisation and mechanistic studies have further enhanced their potential applications. The review covers multifunctional properties of medicinal plant-derived bioactive compounds, particularly their antioxidant, antimicrobial, and corrosion inhibition activities. In addition, the review highlights current challenges, recent advances in green and sustainable approaches, and future perspectives involving nanotechnology and hybrid multifunctional systems.

title: MemBack: An Equivariant Graph Neural Network for Backmapping Lipid Membranes
abstractText: Abstract Backmapping coarse-grained (CG) simulations to atomistic resolution is central to multiscale molecular simulation but remains challenging for chemically complex lipid membranes. We introduce MemBack, an SE(3)-equivariant graph neural network (GNN) that reconstructs CHARMM36 lipid structures from Martini 3 configurations by single-pass heavy-atom prediction followed by automated postprocessing. Across chemically diverse systems, MemBack achieved a mean superposition-free per-lipid heavy-atom RMSD of 0.65 Å while retaining comparable accuracy for membrane systems and lipid species excluded from training. At the membrane scale, MemBack preserved structural organization across resolutions: in a 16-component red-blood-cell (RBC) membrane model excluded from training, bilayer thickness, area per lipid (APL), and acyl-chain order closely matched the atomistic reference after only restrained minimization; in a native phase-separated Martini 3 membrane, the lateral organization of ordered and disordered domains was likewise retained directly after backmapping, without atomistic equilibration. Native Martini 3 systems containing up to 1.4 million reconstructed atoms remained consistent with their parent coarse-grained configurations and could be propagated in atomistic simulations, providing an efficient interface between Martini 3 and CHARMM36 membrane simulations.
