title: A wood-based substrate for passive humidity buffering and visual humidity indication in museum display cases
abstractText: Eco-friendly wood-based substrates that combine passive humidity buffering with visual humidity indication remain limited for museum display cases. Poplar wood was modified by low-temperature ultrasonic co-impregnation with glycerol and anthocyanin. Substrate screening, single-factor experiments and orthogonal experiments were used to optimise additive dosage and impregnation time. Scanning electron microscopy (SEM) and Fourier transform infra-red spectroscopy (FTIR) indicated that modification was governed mainly by pore filling and intermolecular hydrogen bonding. The optimal process used 22 w/w% glycerol, 0.6 w/w% anthocyanin and 9 h impregnation, yielding a 51% higher 24 h moisture uptake than untreated poplar, with effective pore filling and uniform pigment dispersion. The colour response remained detectable after 30 wet–dry cycles. This work provides an environmentally compatible wood-based substrate for supplementary passive humidity buffering and close-range visual humidity indication in museum display cases.

title: Numerical modelling of deformation-induced reflection response in electromagnetic meta-surfaces
abstractText: Communication systems for advanced wireless networks such as innovative air mobility look towards electromagnetic meta-materials in order to facilitate a safe and reliable communication infrastructure. Despite significant advancements in computational electromagnetism, current literature lacks a systematic simulation framework considering multi-physical effects on the electromagnetic response. Physical experiments on the effects of the varying environmental conditions such as temperature, moisture, wind and strains of the host surface on the electromagnetic response of these devices are limited by the high costs of planning, frequency band licensing and outdoor environment emulators. This study proposes a sequentially coupled simulation framework to compute the electromagnetic far-field scattered by such an electromagnetic meta-material, subject to deformation induced by external factors. The changes in the bi-static scattering cross-section due to deformation are studied by defining shape and directionality metrics under different deformation amplitudes and panel dimensions. Analysis reveals a higher sensitivity of the electromagnetic response to the deformation amplitude as opposed to the number of unit cells deployed.

title: Fatigue assessment of welded top flange to web junctions of crane runway beams subject to concentrated wheel loads
abstractText: The fatigue design of heavily loaded crane runway girders is significantly influenced by the fatigue classification of welded top flange-to-web junctions subjected to concentrated wheel loads. The current classification according to EN 1993‐1-9 is considerably more conservative than previous German design provisions and other international standards. To investigate the fatigue resistance of these details, 66 crane runway girders subjected to several decades of heavy service loading were examined in the field. Only three girders showed fatigue damage at the investigated welded connections, while the remaining girders exhibited no identified fatigue damage despite their extensive loading histories. The field data were evaluated using a maximum likelihood approach accounting for both damaged girders and runouts. Additional numerical investigations based on effective notch stresses and multiaxial fatigue assessment were conducted to evaluate the influence of weld geometry and plate thickness. Based on the combined investigations, supplementary fatigue classes ranging from FAT 71 to FAT 140 are proposed for different weld configurations and execution requirements. The results provide a basis for a more differentiated and economical fatigue assessment of welded top flange-to-web junctions in heavy-duty crane runway girders.

title: Aeroallergen sensitisation patterns in adults with rhinitis and asthma: insights from the Middle Black Sea region of Türkiye
abstractText: Aeroallergen sensitisation varies geographically and may be influenced by environmental and climatic factors. Understanding regional sensitisation patterns is important for allergy assessment and management. However, contemporary clinical data from the Middle Black Sea region of Türkiye are limited. This study aimed to describe aeroallergen sensitisation patterns in adults with rhinitis and/or asthma undergoing allergy evaluation and to explore their relationship with clinical phenotype and asthma severity. This retrospective cross-sectional study included 754 adults with rhinitis and/or asthma undergoing allergy evaluation who underwent skin prick testing at a tertiary allergy clinic between January 2023 and October 2024. Sensitisation profiles were analysed according to demographic characteristics, disease phenotype, and retrospectively assigned GINA treatment-step categories as a proxy for asthma severity. Multivariable multinomial logistic regression analysis was performed to evaluate the association between major aeroallergen sensitisation groups and GINA treatment-step categories, with Steps 1–2 as the reference category and adjustment for age, sex, and the other major allergen sensitisation groups. Overall, 377 patients (50.0%) were sensitized to at least one aeroallergen, and 53.8% of sensitized individuals showed polysensitisation. Among the 377 sensitized patients, pollen was the most common allergen group (60.5%), followed by mite sensitisation (50.9%), animal dander (44.6%), moulds (24.9%), latex (21.0%), and cockroach (18.3%). Among individual allergens, Dermatophagoides pteronyssinus (35.3%) and Dermatophagoides farinae (28.6%) were the predominant sensitizers. Cockroach sensitisation was significantly more frequent in patients with concomitant rhinitis and asthma than in those with rhinitis without asthma. Across the full GINA treatment-step strata, mite sensitisation was more frequent in Steps 1–2 than in Step 5 (45.5% [15/33] vs. 18.2% [16/88], p = 0.002). In multivariable multinomial logistic regression analysis adjusted for age and sex, the Step 5 category was associated with lower odds of mite sensitisation than the Steps 1–2 category (OR 0.29, 95% CI 0.11–0.81; p = 0.02). In this tertiary allergy clinic cohort of adults with rhinitis and/or asthma in the Middle Black Sea coastal region of Türkiye, 50.0% had SPT-defined sensitisation to at least one tested aeroallergen. Among sensitized individuals, mites and pollens were frequently identified, and polysensitisation was common. The exploratory association between mite sensitisation and lower treatment-step categories requires cautious interpretation, as retrospective GINA treatment-step assignment does not establish a fully verified asthma-severity phenotype. These findings may help inform the composition of region-specific allergen testing panels; however, the study did not evaluate diagnostic accuracy, and positive SPT results require demonstration of clinical relevance before allergen-specific management. Not applicable.

title: Azithromycin use in pediatric pityriasis lichenoides: a brief retrospective review
abstractText: Abstract Pityriasis Lichenoides Chronica (PLC) and Pityriasis Lichenoides et Varioliformis Acuta (PLEVA) are rare conditions characterized by inflammatory skin lesions with unclear etiology [1,2]. Standard treatments include antibiotics, steroids, methotrexate, and phototherapy [1,3,4,5]. This retrospective chart review compares azithromycin to other standard treatments to assess its safety and effectiveness. Results demonstrated no detectable difference from standard treatments, with the additional advantage of less frequent dosing.

title: Long-term epidemiology of haemorrhagic fever with renal syndrome across three endemic clusters in Jiangxi Province, China’s middle Yangtze River region, 2005–2024
abstractText: Abstract Background Haemorrhagic fever with renal syndrome (HFRS) burden and epidemiological patterns vary across endemic areas of Jiangxi Province. We compared long-term epidemiological patterns in three predefined clusters and explored county-level incidence changes following vaccination-programme initiation. Methods This retrospective ecological study analysed surveillance and population data for 27 counties during 2005–2024. We described burden and seasonality, assessed annual trends with Joinpoint regression, and examined observed age-specific rates alongside complementary age–period–cohort (APC) summaries. In an exploratory analysis of adults aged 15–59 years across all 27 counties, we estimated the average treatment effect on the treated (ATT) over a balanced event-year 0–4 window using the Callaway–Sant’Anna group-time estimator. Counties received equal observation weights; not-yet-initiating and non-initiating counties served as comparisons. Results Across the clusters, 7,570 HFRS cases were reported. Mean annual crude incidence was 7.00, 2.43, and 1.25 per 100,000 person-years in Clusters I–III, respectively; corresponding Segi-standardised rates were 6.29, 2.03, and 1.09. All three clusters had winter peaks, with additional May–June elevations in Clusters I and II. Only Cluster I showed a statistically significant decline in age-standardised incidence over 2005–2024 (average annual percentage change − 4.28%; 95% confidence interval [CI] − 7.27 to − 2.18). Adults aged ≥ 60 years had the highest incidence among the three broad age groups in each cluster, and incidence in this group increased on average in Cluster III. APC period rate ratios were lower in 2020–2024 than in 2010–2014 across all three clusters, with non-linear cohort variation identified in Cluster I. The vaccination-programme initiation ATT among adults aged 15–59 years was − 1.208 cases per 100,000 (95% CI − 1.994 to − 0.421). Conclusions HFRS burden, seasonality, and age-specific incidence differed across the three clusters. Vaccination-programme initiation was associated with lower county-level incidence in the exploratory analysis. These findings support surveillance and prevention tailored to local burden and seasonal patterns, with continued attention to adults aged ≥ 60 years.

title: Topology-Based Generation of Hypothetical Metal−Organic Frameworks through Single-Metal Nodes and Symmetry-Aware Linker Rotation
abstractText: Abstract Topology-based hypothetical metal−organic framework (MOF) generators enable scalable exploration of chemical space beyond experimentally reported structures, but their accessible design space is constrained by the building blocks and assembly rules they encode. Here, we present PORMAKE2, an upgraded topology-based hypothetical MOF generator designed to improve both access to small-pore structures and geometric fidelity. PORMAKE2 introduces an expanded building-block library, including single-metal nodes, and implements symmetry-aware linker rotation for higher-fidelity framework assembly. These upgrades substantially expand the accessible small-pore MOF space and enable MOF designs that were inaccessible to earlier workflows, including ZIF-type and CALF-20-like structures with improved geometrical agreement. Carbon dioxide direct air capture (DAC) and xenon/krypton separation are included as case studies demonstrating that an improved framework-generation workflow can influence downstream screening outcomes. These results establish PORMAKE2 as a more expressive and chemically faithful front-end platform for hypothetical MOF generation.

title: From London to Morse via Binnig, Quate, and Gerber
abstractText: Summary In their landmark paper introducing the atomic force microscope [Phys. Rev. Lett. 56 , 930 (1986)], Binnig, Quate, and Gerber presciently anticipated that the technique would ultimately be capable of probing interactions running the gamut from weak van der Waals interactions to strong covalent bonding. They also highlighted that the tip‐sample forces central to AFM are present, and often highly influential, in scanning tunnelling microscopy; indeed, this realisation directly inspired the invention of the force microscope. In this perspective for the Forty Years of AFM special issue, we review selected aspects of two decades of work from our group at the University of Nottingham that span the force range highlighted by BQG and are united by a common, central theme: the probe as active participant rather than passive observer. Our selection of results also covers length and correlation scales from the microscopic right down to the single chemical bond limit, tracking a spectrum of interactions from van der Waals/Hamaker forces, through hydrogen bonding, to covalent bonds and, finally, atom‐by‐atom assembly of metal clusters via vertical tip‐sample transfer. Echoing BQG's own observations on the prevalence of probe‐sample forces in STM, we also discuss recent evidence that tip‐induced heterogeneity underpins first‐passage dynamics in molecular diffusion and highlight the challenges in acquiring non‐invasive measurements of diffusion barriers for adsorbed molecules that are readily perturbed by the probe. We close with a perspective on machine learning's growing role in automating tip‐driven atomic and molecular manipulation.

title: Machine Learning-Enabled Composition Optimization and Industrial Production of Heat-Treatment-Free High-Strength Ductile Iron
abstractText: Abstract Achieving high strength and adequate ductility in as-cast ductile iron without heat treatment remains a major challenge. In this work, a machine learning-assisted alloy design strategy integrating orthogonal experiments and ensemble learning was developed to establish composition-property relationships for composition optimization. Based on the optimized design and advanced casting technologies, including fully automatic cored-wire feeding spheroidization process, and triple inoculation, a heat-treatment-free high-strength ductile iron was successfully developed. The optimized alloy achieved a tensile strength of 974 MPa, a yield strength of 613 MPa, and an elongation of 6.2% in the as-cast state. Eliminating conventional heat treatment substantially reduces manufacturing time, energy consumption, and production cost while maintaining excellent mechanical performance. This work demonstrates the effectiveness of data-driven alloy design for developing high-performance ductile irons and provides a practical pathway toward sustainable and intelligent cast iron manufacturing.

title: GenOR‐Twin: a semantic middleware for integrating operational discourse with mathematical optimization
abstractText: Abstract We introduce GenOR‐Twin, a neuro‐symbolic framework that bridges the translation gap between unstructured operational logs and rigorous mathematical optimization. Our architecture uniquely positions large language models as semantic translators rather than direct solvers, ensuring that the system retains the feasibility guarantees of exact combinatorial methods. We design a dynamic constraint injection mechanism (the runtime translation of qualitative disruption events into formal mathematical constraints) that allows the system to structurally modify the optimization problem's feasibility region in real time based on qualitative human inputs. The resulting bidirectional coupling—where operational observations update the virtual model state and optimized decisions are reflected back into the knowledge graph—satisfies the synchronization requirement of a proper digital twin. The framework features an adaptive decision policy that automatically selects between low‐complexity schedule repair and full re‐optimization by analyzing the available system slack. Finally, we demonstrate the generalization of this approach across six distinct optimization domains, showing that static models can adapt to real‐world operational uncertainty.

title: Polaris: A toolkit for standardized construction, integration, and quantitative testing in Escherichia coli and Saccharomyces cerevisiae
abstractText: Existing synthetic biology toolkits have expanded part libraries and assembly capabilities. However, new users may still encounter ambiguity in construct definitions, hierarchical transitions, genomic integration routes, and quantitative testing procedures. Here, we present Polaris, a Golden Gate toolkit for Escherichia coli and Saccharomyces cerevisiae . Polaris uses a MoClo-derived three-level hierarchy. Level 1 stores reusable parts, Level 2 generates transcription units and other intermediate constructs, and Level 3 supports multigene assembly and switching between testing and integration backbones. The toolkit distinguishes part interfaces from transcription unit interfaces, uses Bpi I and Bsa I in successive assembly stages, and provides parallel ccdB and mScarletI3 screening options. Integration modules and quantitative characterization frameworks were implemented in both hosts and demonstrated using representative genetic parts and activation and repression systems. A companion digital platform further encodes the Level 1 to Level 3 rules for assembly planning. Polaris connects hierarchical construction, stable genetic implementation, and quantitative testing within a common execution framework, providing a practical basis for data accumulation, part standardization, and future automation.

title: Automated quantification of the meiotic spindle-polar body angle and its association with embryo euploidy
abstractText: Non-invasive assessment of embryo euploidy from oocyte-derived parameters remains a major challenge in assisted reproduction. Oocyte meiotic competence is closely associated with embryo ploidy. Our proof-of-concept study establishes a methodology for identifying a laboratory-specific meiotic spindle-polar body (MS-PB) angle range in which embryo euploidy is more frequent than outside this range. MS-PB angles were automatically quantified from polarized light microscopy photographs and videos using a U-Net-based deep learning model. Oocytes clinically classified as metaphase II (MII) were recorded ~ 40 h after trigger administration. The final analysis included 81 oocytes with an evaluable MS-PB angle and an available PGT-A result from the corresponding embryo. Embryos derived from oocytes within the exploratory laboratory-specific MS-PB angle range (8-32°) exhibited significantly higher euploidy rates than those outside this interval (72.2% vs. 31.1%; p = 0.000236). Patient-clustered binary logistic regression showed 5.76-fold higher odds of euploidy within this range (OR = 5.76, 95% CI 2.03-16.31; p = 0.00098). Exploratory ROC analysis yielded an AUC of 0.725, further supporting the association between the MS-PB angle and embryo ploidy. Our findings demonstrate the potential of automated MS-PB angle measurement to provide information on corresponding embryo ploidy.

title: Invisible Wounds: Structural Violence and Institutional Power in 4.48 Psychosis and Cleansed
abstractText: This paper examines Sarah Kane's plays Cleansed (1998) and 4.48 Psychosis (2000) through the lens of structural violence and institutional power. Drawing on Johan Galtung's concept of structural violence as indirect harm embedded in social systems, it argues that Kane depicts "invisible wounds", psychological, emotional, and existential traumas inflicted by oppressive institutions such as psychiatric facilities and authoritarian regimes. In Cleansed, the institution manifests as a site of physical torture and identity erasure, reflecting broader societal mechanisms of control over non-normative bodies and desires. In 4.48 Psychosis, violence is internalized, critiquing the medical-industrial complex's failure to address mental suffering. Through fragmented dramaturgy and graphic imagery, Kane exposes how institutional power perpetuates harm, urging audiences to confront complicity in these systems. This analysis synthesizes trauma theory, Postdramatic theatre, and feminist critiques to illuminate Kane's contribution to experiential.

title: Association between CPAK phenotype alteration and changes in coronal ankle alignment after restricted kinematic alignment total knee arthroplasty: a retrospective cohort study
abstractText: Abstract Background: Changes in coronal knee alignment after total knee arthroplasty may influence distal lower-limb biomechanics and ankle alignment. The coronal plane alignment of the knee (CPAK) classification provides a framework for describing knee phenotypes based on arithmetic hip-knee-ankle angle (aHKA) and joint line obliquity (JLO). This study investigated whether postoperative CPAK phenotype alteration was associated with changes in coronal ankle alignment after restricted kinematic alignment (rKA) total knee arthroplasty. Methods: This retrospective cohort study included 152 patients who underwent primary unilateral total knee arthroplasty using a restricted kinematic alignment strategy between January 2023 and December 2025. Standing long-leg and ankle radiographs were obtained preoperatively and at 6 months postoperatively. Patients were classified into CPAK-preserved and CPAK-altered groups according to whether the postoperative CPAK phenotype was identical to the preoperative phenotype. Coronal ankle alignment was assessed using tibial plafond inclination (TPI), talar inclination (TI), and talar tilt (TT). Postoperative ankle pain and the influence of preoperative coronal deformity severity were also evaluated. Results: Among 152 knees, 103 knees (67.8%) showed postoperative CPAK phenotype alteration, whereas 49 knees (32.2%) preserved the preoperative CPAK phenotype. Baseline demographic characteristics were comparable between groups. No significant between-group differences were observed in preoperative or postoperative TPI, TI, or TT. Changes in TPI, TI, and TT were also not significantly different between groups; the altered-minus-preserved mean differences were 0.00 degrees (95% CI, -0.18 to 0.19), -0.80 degrees (95% CI, -1.68 to 0.07), and -0.05 degrees (95% CI, -0.20 to 0.10), respectively. Postoperative ankle pain occurred in 19 patients (12.5%) and was not more frequent in the CPAK-altered group or in patients with preoperative coronal deformity greater than 10 degrees. Conclusions: In patients undergoing rKA total knee arthroplasty, postoperative CPAK phenotype alteration was common, but no statistically significant between-group differences were detected in directional changes in coronal ankle alignment or in postoperative ankle pain at 6 months. However, the confidence interval for TI change did not exclude a modest difference.

title: Theoretical research on tetrazine-based nitrogen-chain energetic materials: balancing detonation performance and sensitivity via structural regulation
abstractText: Abstract Context Herein, we proposed a strategy using a 1,2,3,4-tetrazine ring as the molecular skeleton to construct nitrogen-chain frameworks. A series of tetrazine-based molecules (Series I - IV ) were designed and investigated via DFT calculations. The tetrazine-based scaffold retained high nitrogen content and density while offering enhanced thermodynamic stability over triazole-based analogues. Over half of the designed molecules displayed densities higher than 1.80 g/cm 3 and several derivatives even exceeded 1.90 g/cm 3 (1.902–1.965 g/cm 3 ). Predicted detonation velocities (8.926–11.32 km/s) and pressures (33.94–59.18 GPa) surpassed those of triazole-based analogues and HOF (948.8–1951 kJ/mol) were markedly higher. This work established a theoretical framework that may guide the rational design and experimental synthesis of next-generation insensitive high-energy materials. Method Geometry optimizations and frequency analyses were carried out with Gaussian 09 using the B3PW91/6‑311 + G(d,p) and M06‑2X/6‑311 + G(d,p) method, respectively. Isodesmic reactions were employed to obtain heat of formation (HOF), while Multiwfn 3.8_dev software was used for calculations of HOMO-LUMO energy gaps (ΔE), electrostatic potentials (ESP) and other relevant descriptors. Weak intermolecular interactions in the dimers were visualized via VMD 1.9.3 program.

title: Efficacy and safety of fecal microbiota transplantation in children with refractory functional abdominal pain disorders: an open-label pilot trial with exploratory microbiome analyses
abstractText: Abstract Background Fecal microbiota transplantation (FMT) rebuilds the gut microbiota, yet its efficacy in pediatric refractory functional abdominal pain disorders (FAPDs) is insufficiently described. The purpose of this study is to identify gut microbiota dysbiosis in pediatric FAPDs and to examine the effectiveness, safety, and microbial biomarkers of FMT in these patients. Methods In a two-phase study, gut microbiota (16 S rRNA sequencing) were compared between 47 children with FAPDs and 39 healthy controls. Thereafter, a non-randomized, open-label prospective pilot trial (ClinicalTrials.gov: NCT05753774) allocated the 47 refractory patients, according to guardian and/or patient preference, to receive FMT plus conventional therapy ( n = 26) or conventional therapy only ( n = 21). The trial was terminated early because of slow recruitment (47 of 50 planned participants). The primary endpoint was the composite response rate at weeks 4 and 8. Results At baseline, patients had significant gut microbiota dysbiosis: 3.5-fold Proteobacteria enrichment (20.6% vs. 5.8%; P < 0.001), 4.1-fold Escherichia–Shigella expansion (12.7% vs. 3.1%; P < 0.001), and reduced α-diversity (Shannon index 4.7 ± 1.1 vs. 5.4 ± 1.1; P = 0.002). FMT plus conventional therapy was associated with a higher composite response rate at week 4 (69.2% vs. 14.3%; RR 4.85, 95% CI 1.65–14.24; Fisher’s exact P < 0.001) and week 8 (80.8% vs. 47.6%; RR 1.70, 95% CI 1.04–2.76; P = 0.029), with significantly better adjusted symptom scores in the FMT group at both time points. Post-FMT, Faecalibacterium and Blautia increased (+ 44.5% and + 99.1%), while Escherichia–Shigella declined (− 19.2%). Exploratory random forest models (seven genera for diagnosis; four genera characterizing the post-FMT, response-associated microbial signature) yielded internally validated AUCs of 0.896 (95% CI 0.821–0.952) and 0.890 (95% CI 0.699–1.000), respectively. FMT showed favorable short-term tolerability, with transient constipation in 50.0% of patients and no severe adverse events. Conclusions In this open-label pilot trial, FMT plus conventional therapy was associated with higher short-term response rates that were maintained through week 8 in children with refractory FAPDs. Exploratory microbial signatures further demonstrated potential for both diagnosis and characterization of the post-treatment, response-associated microbial state, and pending external validation. Trial registration: This study is registered at ClinicalTrials.gov on 11 February 2023 (registration number: NCT05753774), before the enrollment of the first participant. https://clinicaltrials.gov/study/NCT05753774

title: Chemical characterization, antibacterial activity, in vitro cytotoxicity, and selectivity of the lipid extract from Sargassum filipendula against multidrug-resistant bacteria
abstractText: Antimicrobial resistance in multidrug-resistant (MDR) bacteria necessitates new therapeutic alternatives, and marine macroalgae represent an underexplored source of bioactive lipids. This study characterized the lipid extract (LE) of Sargassum filipendula and evaluated its antibacterial and cytotoxic profiles against MDR hospital isolates. LE composition was determined by GC-MS, and its thermal behavior by thermogravimetric analysis (TGA) and differential scanning calorimetry (DSC). Antibacterial activity was evaluated using the broth microdilution method (CLSI M07) against Acinetobacter baumannii , Escherichia coli , Klebsiella pneumoniae , Pseudomonas aeruginosa , Staphylococcus aureus , and coagulase-negative staphylococci, followed by determination of the minimum bactericidal concentration. Cytotoxicity was assessed in L929 and MDBK cell lines using MTT, Neutral Red, and Lactate Dehydrogenase assays; Hemolytic activity was evaluated using erythrocytes; and selectivity indices (SI) were calculated for each bacterial species. Palmitic acid (61.07%) and oleic acid (15.90%) were the predominant fatty acids. TGA revealed a total mass loss of 82% across two decomposition stages (296 °C, 445 °C), and DSC detected no phase transitions between − 80 and 270 °C. The LE exhibited bacteriostatic activity against all isolates, with MIC values ranging from 1.18 mg/mL ( S. aureus ) to 2.5 mg/mL ( P. aeruginosa ). Cytotoxicity assays yielded IC 50 values ranging from 0.16 to 1.25 mg/mL, and the hemolytic IC 50 was 12.81 mg/mL. However, assay-specific SI values were ≤ 1.06 for adherent cells and 5.12–10.86 for erythrocytes. The S. filipendula LE is a candidate source of antibacterial compounds against MDR bacteria, although purification processes and in vivo validation are required to establish its therapeutic potential.

title: Bacterial profile, antimicrobial susceptibility patterns, and associated factors of lower respiratory tract infections among adult patients attending Nekemte Comprehensive Specialized Hospital: a cross-sectional study
abstractText: Lower respiratory tract infections are among the leading causes of illnesses responsible for causing death and adding significant costs to the public health system. Bacteria are the most common causative agents of lower respiratory tract infections. Currently, there is little information on the prevalence, antimicrobial susceptibility patterns, and associated factors of lower respiratory tract infections among adult patients in Ethiopia. Therefore, the objective of this study was to determine prevalence of lower respiratory tract infection, antimicrobial susceptibility profiles and associated factors in the study area. A laboratory-based cross-sectional study was conducted among 376 participants at Nekemte Comprehensive Specialized Hospital from June to September 2024. A structured questionnaire was used to gather sociodemographic and clinical data. Bacterial isolation and identification were done using standard microbiological techniques. The Kirby-Bauer disc diffusion method was used to perform antibiotic susceptibility testing. Data were entered into Epi Data v4.6 and exported to the Statistical Package for Social Science (SPSS) v24 for analysis. Logistic regression analysis was done to assess the association between dependent and independent variables. The strength and significance of the association were determined by adjusted odds ratio (AOR) and p-value ˂ 0.05, respectively. Finally, the results were presented using text, tables, and figures. Of 376 sputum samples from adult patients with lower respiratory tract infection, 195 (51.9%) were culture-positive for bacterial pathogens. One hundred ninety-seven bacteria were isolated, with Gram-negative and Gram-positive bacteria accounting for 147 (74.6%) and 50 (25.4%), respectively. Klebsiella pneumoniae (19.8%) was the predominant bacterial isolate, followed by Pseudomonas aeruginosa (17.8%). Gram-negative bacteria were more sensitive to both ciprofloxacin (78.9%) and piperacillin-tazobactam (78.9%), while Gram-positive isolates were sensitive to clindamycin (96.0%). Age, educational status, marital status and occupation had a statistically significant association with lower respiratory tract infections (LRTIs) with a p-value of < 0.05. Klebsiella pneumoniae was the predominant isolate of the lower respiratory tract infection pathogen followed by P. aeruginosa . Most isolates of bacteria were resistant to commonly prescribed antibiotics. A significant association was observed with age, educational status, marital status, and occupation. Culture and antibiotic susceptibility testing is essential before treatment to limit the possibility of antimicrobial resistance. Not applicable.

title: Intraoperative technology in skull base and vascular neurosurgery: a two-stage cross-sectional national survey
abstractText: Abstract Skull base and vascular neurosurgery rely on diverse intraoperative technologies, but contemporary data describing how frequently they are used at the level of individual operations are limited. On behalf of the Society of British Neurological Surgeons (SBNS) MedTech Committee, we aimed to establish a dated descriptive baseline of reported technology use across three operative paradigms. We conducted a two-stage cross-sectional survey of neurosurgeons in the UK and Ireland via the Society of British Neurological Surgeons (SBNS). Six MedTech Committee members compiled a pragmatic technology list. Respondents reported frequency of use for three exemplar procedures: transsphenoidal pituitary adenoma, retrosigmoid vestibular schwannoma, and pterional aneurysm surgery. Use was recorded on a four-point ordinal scale and analysed descriptively, with Kendall’s tau-b used to explore the relationship between experience and reported use. Twenty-four responses from 20 of the 32 adult or mixed adult-paediatric UK units were analysed (11 units per index procedure). Reported use was strongly procedure specific. Neuronavigation was used always or almost always by 8/12 transsphenoidal respondents but infrequently elsewhere. Endoscopy had displaced microscopy in transsphenoidal surgery, whereas microscopy was used always or almost always by all retrosigmoid and pterional respondents. Indocyanine green and micro-Doppler were routine for aneurysms. Neurophysiological monitoring was universal for vestibular schwannoma but evenly divided for aneurysms. Exoscopes, intraoperative MRI and robotics were used infrequently or not at all; augmented reality was reported by 5/13 pterional respondents. No association was found between experience and reported use, though this was underpowered. Reported intraoperative technology use is strongly shaped by operative paradigm, with established technologies clustering around recurring procedural needs. Newer technologies were used infrequently. Because availability was not recorded, non-use cannot be distinguished from lack of access. These data provide a dated baseline against which future change can be assessed.

title: Effect of plastic deformation on corrosion, biological and technological properties of anodized Ti6Al4V ELI implants
abstractText: Abstract Electrochemical anodization improves the surface properties of titanium implants, but the resulting oxide layer may be damaged by plastic deformation during insertion or service. This study investigated how four deformation levels, together with an undeformed reference, affect anodized Ti6Al4V ELI. Surface morphology, roughness, wettability, microstructure, cytocompatibility, and electrochemical behavior were evaluated. Deformation progressively increased surface roughness and induced micro- and macrocracking of the anodic layer, while all surfaces remained hydrophilic. Damage to the oxide markedly reduced corrosion protection: the corrosion rate increased from approx. 50 to 650 nm year⁻¹, whereas polarization resistance decreased from 11,920 to 327 kΩ·cm². Electrochemical impedance spectroscopy indicated facilitated ionic transport through deformation-induced defects. Nevertheless, no cytotoxic effect on MC3T3-E1 cells was observed, and differences in cell viability were not statistically significant. Thus, plastic deformation substantially impairs the electrochemical barrier function of anodized Ti6Al4V ELI without adversely affecting its short-term cytocompatibility.

title: Isolated Langerhans cell histiocytosis of the thyroid gland mimicking thyroid malignancy: a diagnostic pitfall and literature review—a case report
abstractText: Langerhans cell histiocytosis (LCH) is a rare clonal proliferative disorder of dendritic cells characterized by variable clinical manifestations and multisystem involvement. Thyroid involvement is exceptionally uncommon and may clinically mimic primary thyroid malignancy, creating significant diagnostic challenges. We report a rare case of 35-year-old Vietnamese woman, Kinh ethnicity, presenting with a progressively enlarging thyroid mass associated with dysphagia and hoarseness. Her medical history was notable for diabetes insipidus. Ultrasonography (USG) revealed diffuse enlargement of the thyroid gland with a dominant solid nodule in the left lobe. Fine-needle aspiration biopsy (FNAB) suggested a malignant lesion suspicious for lymphoma. The patient subsequently underwent total thyroidectomy for definitive diagnosis and treatment. Histopathological examination demonstrated diffuse infiltration of the thyroid parenchyma by atypical histiocytic cells with characteristic grooved nuclei admixed with numerous eosinophils and lymphocytes. Immunohistochemical analysis revealed strong positivity for CD1a and S100 protein, confirming the diagnosis of Langerhans cell histiocytosis. Further systemic evaluation showed no evidence of extracervical involvement, establishing the diagnosis of isolated thyroid LCH. She was subsequently received adjuvant chemotherapy with cytarabine, along with levothyroxine and remained clinically stable for 6-month follow-up period. Primary thyroid LCH is an exceedingly rare entity that can closely resemble thyroid malignancy both clinically and cytologically. Accurate diagnosis relies heavily on histopathological evaluation and immunohistochemical confirmation. Awareness of this rare diagnostic possibility is important to avoid misdiagnosis and to guide appropriate systemic assessment and management.

title: Low-frequency phase in early visual cortex gates prefrontal influence on perception
IDDA-Scored Abatacept-to-HSCT Course in Pediatric LRBA Deficiency
abstractText: Abstract LRBA deficiency is a rare inborn error of immunity in which impaired CTLA-4 recycling causes immune dysregulation; haematopoietic stem cell transplantation (HSCT) is curative, but no standardised measure of pre-transplant disease activity exists and the role of abatacept as a bridge to HSCT remains ill-defined. We report a 4-year-old girl with compound heterozygous LRBA variants in whom abatacept, given as a planned bridge to transplantation, reduced disease activity within four months (Immune Deficiency and Dysregulation Activity [IDDA] score 54.5 to 22.6), maintained control until transplant, and was followed by an IDDA of 1.0 at 22 months after fully matched unrelated-donor HSCT. Retrospective IDDA scoring was feasible in 32 of 46 published LRBA HSCT patients (22 with and 10 without pre-HSCT abatacept; baseline scores 11.1 vs 11.5), with descriptively higher survival in abatacept-bridged patients (95.8% vs 86.4%; P = 0.34). The IDDA provides a practical metric to quantify disease activity and to evaluate the contribution of pre-HSCT abatacept in LRBA deficiency.

title: Drug Use in Autistic and Non-Autistic Adults: Findings from the Global Drug Survey
abstractText: Background: Autistic people may be at greater risk of developing alcohol and substance use disorders, despite being less likely to use drugs and alcohol overall. Little research has compared autistic and non-autistic adults across multiple drug classes in large international samples. This study aimed to examine patterns, reasons, and risks associated with drug use in autistic and non-autistic people, using survey data from the Global Drug Survey 2022. Methods: Logistic regression models were used to assess differences between autistic ( N = 725) and non-autistic participants ( N = 27,057) in odds of drug use, binge drinking, emergency medical treatment for drug and/or alcohol use, and reasons for use in past 12 months, and negative binomial regression with a log link function for frequency of drug use in days. Covariates in adjusted models were age, gender, ethnicity, and education. Correlations assessed relationships between frequency and impact of autism in daily life. Results: Autistic people had lower odds of using alcohol, cocaine, and cigarettes and greater odds of using prescription opioids compared with non-autistic people in the past 12 months. Of those who used each drug in the past 12 months, autistic respondents used alcohol significantly less frequently and amphetamine/crystal methamphetamine, cannabis, and cannabidiol (CBD) significantly more frequently than non-autistic people. Autistic respondents had greater odds of using cannabis for medical reasons and amphetamine for functional reasons and greater odds of seeking emergency medical treatment for alcohol and/or drug use compared with non-autistic people. There was no association between frequency of drug use and impact of autism. Conclusions: Despite lower odds of using alcohol and cigarettes, autistic people who used drugs did so more frequently for certain substances (amphetamine/methamphetamine, cannabis, and CBD), often for medical or functional reasons. These patterns suggest drug use may serve self-regulatory or coping functions, highlighting a need for tailored harm-reduction support.

title: A Comparative Analysis Of Academic Buoyancy Among Higher Secondary School Students On The Basis Of Gender
abstractText: Academic buoyancy refers to students’ capacity to manage ordinary academic setbacks, such as disappointing marks, examination pressure, difficult assignments, competing deadlines, and critical feedback. The present study examined academic buoyancy among higher secondary school students in relation to gender. A quantitative, cross-sectional, descriptive-comparative design was used. This study reported the sample of 300 students (150 male and 150 female) in Tehsil Sahiwal and Tehsil Shahpur, District Sargodha. Academic buoyancy was measured through a 20-item questionnaire covering composure, confidence, coordination, commitment, and control; the reported pilot reliability was Cronbach’s alpha = .830. The gender table showed that 54.0% of male students, compared with 41.3% of female students, were classified in the upper two buoyancy categories (very good or excellent). A chi-square test of the five-category gender distribution was not statistically significant. The equivalent one-way analysis of variance was also not significant, F (1, 298) = 3.03, p = .083.

title: Drug Repurposing Overcomes the Gram-Negative Permeability Barrier to Expand the Antibacterial Spectrum of MGB-BP-3
abstractText: Abstract The outer membrane of Gram-negative bacteria imposes a formidable barrier to antibacterial agents, severely limiting the efficacy of many novel drug candidates. MGB-BP-3, a DNA minor groove binder, exhibits potent activity against Gram-positive bacteria but has shown limited efficacy against Gram-negative pathogens due to this permeability barrier. The Pandemic Response Box (PRB), a curated library of structurally diverse molecules, provides a resource to identify potential resistance-circumventing compounds that can be repurposed as adjuvants. Here, we screened the PRB for synergy with MGB-BP-3 against Gram-negative priority pathogens. While MGB-BP-3 alone showed minimal in vitro activity, combination testing identified 15 hit compounds, with pafuramidine and sulbactam showing the most synergy against Escherichia coli. To prioritize translatability, we substituted these hits with clinically relevant mechanistic analogues pentamidine and ceftazidime, respectively, which both maintained synergistic activity as measured by Fractional Inhibitory Concentration Indices (FICI < 0.5). Quantitative confocal microscopy using a fluorescent analogue of MGB-BP-3 (S-MGB-245) confirmed that this potentiation was correlated with increased intracellular accumulation of the S-MGB. In vivo efficacy testing using Escherichia coli-infected Galleria mellonella larvae demonstrated significantly improved larval survival with combination therapy compared to monotherapies (p < 0.05). Notably, coadministering subtherapeutic doses of MGB-BP-3 (12.5 mg/kg) with pentamidine (60 mg/kg) or ceftazidime (0.8 mg/kg) achieved ≥75% survival, whereas these exact same concentrations yielded complete mortality when administered individually. These results highlight the potential of clinically used drugs to overcome the intrinsic resistance of Gram-negative bacteria to MGB-BP-3 by compromising the cell envelope, thereby extending the antibacterial spectrum of MGB-BP-3.

title: Preoperative CRP outperforms symptom duration in discriminating severe operative difficulty in acute cholecystitis
abstractText: Abstract Background Operative difficulty during emergency laparoscopic cholecystectomy (ELC) can vary substantially. This study evaluated the independent association of peak pre-operative C-reactive protein (CRP) with operative difficulty and compared discrimination for severe difficulty between CRP- and symptom-duration-based models. Methods A retrospective multicentre cohort study was conducted within Wide Bay Hospital and Health Service (November 2021-May 2024). Adult patients undergoing ELC were included. Operative difficulty was graded 1 to 4 using a validated intra-operative grading system. Ordinal logistic regression evaluated independent associations. Age- and sex-adjusted logistic models containing either CRP or symptom duration were compared using receiver operating characteristic analysis for grade 4 difficulty. Results A total of 284 patients were included. CRP was independently associated with increasing operative difficulty (adjusted OR 2.24 per one-unit increase in ln(CRP), 95% CI 1.91–2.63; p < 0.001), while longer symptom duration was inversely related (adjusted OR 0.81 per day, 95% CI 0.73–0.90; p < 0.001). The CRP model demonstrated greater discrimination than the symptom-duration model (AUC 0.863, 95% CI 0.816–0.910 versus 0.727, 95% CI 0.664–0.790; p < 0.001). A CRP threshold of 92.5 mg/L predicted grade 4 difficulty with 76.2% sensitivity, 82.5% specificity, and 89.2% negative predictive value. Conclusion Higher CRP and shorter symptom duration were independently associated with greater operative difficulty. The CRP model showed better discrimination for grade 4 difficulty within this cohort. CRP may support pre-operative risk stratification and operative planning, subject to validation.

title: Pendampingan Perancangan Sistem Informasi Persuratan Desa Sumberejo Menggunakan Metode Rapid Application Development
abstractText: Pelayanan administrasi surat-menyurat di Desa Sumberejo, Kecamatan Way Jepara, Kabupaten Lampung Timur sebelumnya masih dilakukan secara manual menggunakan arsip fisik, dengan rata-rata 3 hingga 5 permohonan per hari. Kondisi tersebut menimbulkan sejumlah kendala operasional, seperti proses pelayanan yang lambat, kesulitan pencarian dokumen, risiko kerusakan atau kehilangan arsip, serta keterlambatan persetujuan akibat ketergantungan pada kehadiran fisik Kepala Desa. Kegiatan pengabdian kepada masyarakat ini bertujuan mendampingi perangkat Desa Sumberejo dalam proses perencanaan kebutuhan dan perancangan sistem informasi pelayanan surat-menyurat berbasis web menggunakan metode Rapid Application Development (RAD). Metode pelaksanaan dibagi menjadi tiga tahap, yaitu pra pelaksanaan, pelaksanaan, dan evaluasi. Pada tahap pelaksanaan diterapkan pendekatan RAD melalui tahapan requirements planning dan design workshop secara iteratif yang melibatkan langsung perangkat desa sebagai mitra. Hasil kegiatan menunjukkan bahwa tim berhasil mengidentifikasi 8 kebutuhan fungsional sistem, menghasilkan rancangan use case diagram, 7 activity diagram, Entity Relationship Diagram (ERD) dengan 19 entitas, serta 9 rancangan antarmuka low-fidelity untuk tampilan desktop dan mobile. Proses iterasi desain dilaksanakan sebanyak 3 kali bersama mitra hingga rancangan dinyatakan sesuai kebutuhan. Kegiatan ini memberikan kontribusi nyata dalam mempercepat digitalisasi administrasi desa dan menghasilkan fondasi perancangan sistem yang siap dikembangkan lebih lanjut.

title: Analisis Keunggulan Komparatif Ekspor Bahan Bakar Mineral Indonesia ke China Tahun 2018-2025
abstractText: This study aims to analyze the comparative advantage of Indonesian mineral fuel exports to China during the period 2018–2025. Mineral fuels are one of Indonesia's important export commodities and contribute to its international trade relations, particularly with China as one of its major trading partners. This study employs a quantitative descriptive approach using secondary data obtained from Trade Map, covering Indonesia's mineral fuel exports to China, China's mineral fuel imports from the world, and Indonesia's total exports. The data are analyzed using the Revealed Comparative Advantage (RCA) method to identify the comparative advantage of Indonesian mineral fuel exports in the Chinese market. The results show that the value of Indonesian mineral fuel exports to China experienced fluctuations throughout the observation period. Export values increased significantly in 2021 and reached their highest level in 2022, before declining from 2023 to 2025. Furthermore, the RCA values recorded in the dataset remained below 1 throughout the period, ranging from 0.19 to 0.33. These findings indicate that Indonesian mineral fuel exports have not demonstrated a comparative advantage in the Chinese market during the period studied. Therefore, improvements in export competitiveness and market positioning are necessary to strengthen Indonesia's presence in China's mineral fuel market.

title: Mekanisme Artificial Intelligence sebagai Mediator Komunikasi Digital dalam Pengayaan Mufradat Bahasa Arab: Perspektif Konseptual
abstractText: Penguasaan mufradat menentukan kemampuan mahasiswa memahami dan memakai bahasa Arab, tetapi pembelajarannya masih bertumpu pada hafalan yang minim konteks dan lingkungan berbahasa yang terbatas. Artikel ini bertujuan menyusun kerangka konseptual tentang cara kerja artificial intelligence sebagai mediator komunikasi digital dalam pengayaan mufradat bahasa Arab. Kata mediator dibedakan menjadi arti teknis dan pedagogis. Metodenya kajian pustaka kualitatif terhadap 25 sumber dalam dua kelompok, yaitu pemanfaatan artificial intelligence dan chatbot dalam pembelajaran bahasa, serta problematika pembelajaran mufradat, dengan sintesis tematik berlandaskan teori mediasi sosiokultural. Hasilnya berupa mekanisme dua lapis. Lapis teknis mencakup pembacaan maksud pengguna, pengelolaan dialog, dan penyusunan jawaban. Lapis pedagogis mencakup input kontekstual, umpan balik langsung, latihan berulang, suasana tanpa penilaian, dan penarikan bantuan bertahap, dengan guru yang memeriksa jawaban. Batasnya meliputi penilaian pelafalan yang lemah, jawaban yang kadang keliru, dan risiko ketergantungan. Pengajar dapat memakai kerangka ini untuk memutuskan bagian latihan mufradat yang diserahkan kepada artificial intelligence dan bagian yang tetap dipegang manusia. Bukti empiris tentang mufradat bahasa Arab pada pustaka yang ditelaah masih terbatas, sehingga kerangka ini perlu diuji.

title: Efektivitas Pelatihan Lubang Resapan Biopori dalam Meningkatkan Kesadaran Pengelolaan Sampah Organik di Desa Sekaralas Ngawi
abstractText: Penelitian ini bertujuan mendeskripsikan pelaksanaan pelatihan biopori dan menganalisis efektivitasnya dalam meningkatkan kesadaran masyarakat mengenai pengelolaan limbah organik di Desa Sekaralas, Kecamatan Widodaren, Kabupaten Ngawi. Penelitian ini mengaplikasikan pendekatan kualitatif deskriptif dengan metode pengumpulan data meliputi wawancara mendalam, observasi, dan dokumentasi terhadap 15 informan yang dipilih secara tujuan penelitian. Temuan penelitian mengindikasikan bahwa pelatihan yang berfokus pada praktik langsung dapat meningkatkan pemahaman masyarakat tentang fungsi biopori sebagai alat untuk pengelolaan sampah organik dan pemeliharaan air. Selain itu, terdapat perubahan sikap dan perilaku masyarakat yang terlihat dari menurunnya kebiasaan membakar sampah organik, meningkatnya kesadaran mengenai kebersihan lingkungan, serta mulai dilakukannya pemilahan sampah dan pembuatan lubang biopori di area rumah tangga. Keberhasilan pelatihan didorong oleh semangat masyarakat, bantuan pemerintah desa, keikutsertaan tokoh masyarakat, dan penggunaan metode pelatihan yang partisipatif. Namun, kesinambungan penerapan biopori masih memerlukan dukungan dan pemantauan yang berkelanjutan. Pelatihan lubang resapan biopori terbukti berhasil dalam meningkatkan kesadaran masyarakat mengenai pengelolaan sampah organik yang ramah lingkungan dan berkelanjutan.

title: Penguatan Kapasitas Pengelola Desa Golok sebagai Desa Wisata melalui Literasi Digital dan Partisipasi Warga
abstractText: Desa Mekarmaju di Kabupaten Bandung memiliki potensi wisata berbasis kerajinan pandai besi yang pengembangannya memerlukan pengelolaan informasi digital dan partisipasi masyarakat. Kegiatan pengabdian kepada masyarakat ini bertujuan memperkuat kapasitas pengelola Desa Golok dalam memahami pemanfaatan media digital dan peran masyarakat dalam pengembangan desa wisata. Kegiatan dirancang melalui identifikasi kebutuhan mitra, penyusunan materi pelatihan, perancangan praktik dan pembagian peran, serta pemetaan pemahaman awal peserta. Materi pelatihan mencakup konsep desa wisata, penggunaan Google Maps, media sosial, dan WhatsApp Business, serta peran perajin, warga, dan kelompok sadar wisata (Pokdarwis). Pemahaman awal diukur menggunakan pre-test yang terdiri atas sepuluh soal pilihan ganda. Berdasarkan tabel hasil yang disajikan, seluruh 20 responden menjawab dengan benar setiap butir pertanyaan. Hasil tersebut menunjukkan bahwa responden dapat mengenali jawaban yang tepat terhadap konsep-konsep yang diujikan. Namun, hasil pre-test belum dapat menggambarkan keterampilan praktis maupun perubahan pemahaman setelah pelatihan. Evaluasi lanjutan melalui tugas praktik dan pendampingan diperlukan untuk mendukung penerapan media digital serta pembagian peran dalam pengelolaan informasi wisata Desa Golok.

The role of DSM-5 diagnoses and COVID-19–related cognitive appraisals in vaccine refusal: a SCID-5–based cross-sectional study
abstractText: Abstract Background Vaccine refusal remains a major public health challenge. Although previous studies have linked psychiatric symptoms to vaccine hesitancy, nearly all relied on self-report scales rather than clinical diagnoses, and few have jointly examined psychiatric diagnoses alongside pandemic-related cognitive appraisals. This study compared vaccinated and unvaccinated individuals with respect to DSM-5 diagnoses established through a structured clinical interview and their perceptions and attitudes toward COVID-19, aiming to identify the independent predictors of vaccine refusal. Methods In this cross-sectional study, 215 adults attending a family medicine outpatient clinic between July and September 2022 were enrolled: 101 vaccinated (≥ 3 doses) and 114 unvaccinated (0–1 dose). Psychiatric diagnoses were established using the SCID-5-CV, administered face-to-face. Perceptions and attitudes toward the pandemic were assessed with a validated scale. A hierarchical logistic regression was conducted, entering demographic variables, psychiatric diagnoses, and illness perception subscales in sequential blocks. Results The overall prevalence of psychiatric diagnoses did not differ between groups (48.5% vs. 51.8%, p = .635), and the psychiatric diagnosis block did not significantly improve model fit (Δχ² = 13.6, p = .058). In contrast, illness perception variables markedly improved the model (Δχ² = 37.2, p < .001). Stronger COVID-19 conspiracy beliefs (OR = 1.877, 95% CI 1.332–2.643, p < .001) and lower perceived dangerousness of COVID-19 (OR = 0.486, 95% CI 0.306–0.771, p = .002) were the strongest independent predictors of vaccine refusal. Younger age remained a significant predictor across all models (OR = 0.921, p < .001), whereas the association of female sex was attenuated after adding perception variables. The comorbidity of depressive and anxiety disorders was numerically more frequent in the unvaccinated group but remained at the margin of significance ( p = .054). Conclusions Psychiatric diagnoses established through a structured clinical interview were not independent predictors of vaccine refusal, whereas modifiable cognitive appraisals, particularly COVID-19 conspiracy beliefs and low perceived dangerousness of COVID-19, were the strongest predictors. Interventions to reduce vaccine refusal should target attitudinal factors rather than psychiatric diagnoses.

title: Intraoral retrieval of iatrogenically displaced mandibular third molars from the sublingual and submandibular spaces using a lingual mucoperiosteal flap: a retrospective study of 18 patients
abstractText: Abstract Background Iatrogenic displacement of a mandibular third molar or its root fragment into the floor of the mouth is an uncommon but potentially serious complication of third molar extraction. Published experience is largely limited to isolated case reports, and management remains unstandardised. The fragment-size threshold for retrieval, the optimal timing of retrieval, and the diagnostic value of the Y-sign on panoramic radiographs remain unclear. This study reports the outcomes of a lingual mucoperiosteal flap (LMF) approach used for retrieval on the day of presentation in all patients, including those with small fragments, and the frequency of the Y-sign and preoperative anxiety in this cohort. Methods This was a retrospective study of 18 consecutive patients treated for iatrogenic displacement of mandibular third molars or root fragments into the floor of the mouth at a private oral surgery clinic (Art Dentist Dental Clinic, Hanoi, Vietnam). Treatment and follow-up took place between January 2023 and December 2025. Patients were included if displacement was confirmed clinically and by cone-beam computed tomography, and all were managed with the same LMF approach with a minimum follow-up of 6 months. Results Mean patient age was 26.72 ± 5.88 years, with a slight male predominance (55.56%). Most displaced fragments were roots (94.44%), with a median size of 4.00 mm, and 88.89% of accidents occurred during extraction by general dental practitioners. The Y-sign was present in all 7 patients with available pre-extraction panoramic radiographs (100%). Retrieval was successful in all 18 patients (100%, 95% confidence interval [CI]: 81.47–100), with a median operating time of 22.50 min. No new neurosensory deficit was detected on non-blinded pin-prick testing (0%, 95% CI: 0.00–18.53), and both pre-existing deficits resolved within 5 months. Conclusions In this study, retrieval through an LMF was successful in all 18 patients, and no new neurosensory deficit was detected on non-blinded assessment. The Y-sign is an exploratory observation that merits further study. These findings derive from a single-centre, retrospective study without a comparison group and should be interpreted as hypothesis-generating. Larger prospective studies are needed before broader clinical adoption.

title: PENERAPAN MODEL PROBLEM BASED LEARNING UNTUK MENINGKATKAN KEMAMPUAN NUMERASI MURID PADA PEMBELAJARAN MATEMATIKA MATERI SATUAN PANJANG DAN BERAT KELAS III SD
abstractText: Penelitian ini bertujuan meningkatkan kemampuan numerasi murid melalui penggunaan Problem Based Learning (PBL) dalam materi satuan panjang dan berat pada pelajaran Matematika kelas III sekolah dasar. Penelitian ini dilakukan dengan metode Penelitian Tindakan Kelas (PTK) yang dilakukan selama dua siklus dengan murid berjumlah 30. Setiap siklus memiliki alur pembelajaran yang sama yaitu perencanaan, aksi, pengamatan, dan refleksi. Data dikumpulkan melalui tes, observasi, dan dokumentasi selama pembelajaran. Hasil penelitian yang didapat memperlihatkan terdapat perkembangan hasil penilaian murid siklus I senilai 2.331 dari maksimal skor 3.240 atau 71,94% berkategori cukup, yang berkembang pada siklus II yaitu senilai 2.694 atau 83,15% berkategori baik. Nilai rata-rata pada aspek kognitif berkembang dari 72,67 menjadi 83,33. Perkembangan aspek-aspek yang dinilai dalam penelitian ini mengungkapkan bahwa penggunaan model pembelajaran PBL dapat memberikan hasil yang baik dalam pembelajaran Matematika materi satuan panjang dan berat. Model PBL dinilai mampu menjadi solusi bagi murid dalam mencerna konsep matematika, menyelesaikan masalah sehari-hari, diskusi, dan masalah kontekstual lainnya. Maka dari itu, PBL dinilai memiliki potensi dalam meningkatkan kemampuan numerasi murid sekolah dasar.

Minat Mahasiswa Universitas Muhammadiyah Sumatera Utara terhadap Pengeluaran Menggunakan QRIS dan Tunai di Café Celesco Mukhtar Basri Medan
abstractText: Tujuan dari penelitian ini adalah untuk mengetahui minat mahasiswa Universitas Muhammadiyah Sumatera Utara terhadap penggunaan QRIS dan pembayaran tunai serta hubungannya dengan cara mereka membelanjakan uang di Café Celesco Mukhtar Basri Medan. Dalam penelitian ini, metode kualitatif deskriptif diterapkan pada subjek penelitian, yaitu mahasiswa yang pernah bertransaksi di kafe tersebut. Data dikumpulkan melalui observasi langsung, dan informan dipilih melalui teknik purposive sampling. Hasil penelitian menunjukkan bahwa mahasiswa memiliki minat yang sama terhadap QRIS dan tunai, dan keduanya digunakan bersama dalam transaksi sehari-hari. Sejalan dengan Technology Acceptance Model, QRIS praktis, cepat, mudah digunakan, dan memudahkan pencatatan biaya melalui riwayat transaksi. Pembayaran tunai tetap menjadi pilihan utama siswa karena kemudahan, kebiasaan, kenyamanan, dan ketersediaan saldo digital dan uang tunai. Ini juga menjadi alternatif ketika saldo digital tidak cukup atau jaringan terganggu. Sementara QRIS dapat mengurangi kesadaran tentang jumlah uang yang dibelanjakan, terutama untuk transaksi kecil, tunai memberikan gambaran yang lebih langsung tentang pengeluaran. Namun, metode pembayaran tidak secara langsung mempengaruhi jumlah yang dihabiskan. Pengeluaran sehari-hari lebih bergantung pada kebiasaan dan kemampuan mengelola keuangan, seperti membuat anggaran, mengendalikan diri, dan memeriksa transaksi.

Growth and Yield Responses of Brinjal (Solanum melongena L.) to Increasing Levels of Soil Arsenic Contamination
abstractText: Soil arsenic contamination threatens vegetable production in South Asia, yet the dose-dependent response of brinjal (Solanum melongena L.) to elevated soil arsenate [As(V)] remains insufficiently quantified. A pot experiment was conducted at Sher-e-Bangla Agricultural University, Dhaka, Bangladesh, using a Completely Randomized Design with four replications to evaluate the effects of sodium arsenate (T₁:0, T2:25, T3:50, and T4:75 mg As kg⁻¹ soil) on S. melongena cv. BARI Brinjal 5. Arsenate exposure progressively inhibited vegetative growth, root development, biomass accumulation, and reproductive yield, with peak phytotoxicity observed at 75 mg As kg⁻¹ soil. Compared with the control, the 75 mg As kg⁻¹ treatment significantly reduced root length by 61.7%, root dry weight by 54.2%, plant height by 39.6%, leaf number by 29.2%, and stem diameter by 27.8%, alongside a 32.9% decline in shoot dry weight. Reproductive traits were similarly impaired, reducing individual fruit weight by 34.6% and total fruit yield per plant from ~1.4 kg to ~0.3 kg. These findings demonstrate that soil arsenate severely compromises brinjal productivity; thus, proper soil management and suitable cultivation practices need to be adopted for sustainable vegetable production in arsenic affected areas.

abstractText: Kemampuan pemecahan masalah matematis merupakan kompetensi penting yang harus dimiliki siswa dalam pembelajaran matematika. Namun, hasil observasi di SMA Negeri 2 Mandrehe menunjukkan bahwa kemampuan tersebut masih tergolong rendah. Observasi awal menunjukkan bahwa pembelajaran masih berpusat pada guru dan sebagian siswa mengalami kesulitan menyelesaikan soal yang berbeda dari contoh. Penelitian ini bertujuan untuk mengetahui pengaruh model pembelajaran kontekstual berbasis proyek terhadap kemampuan pemecahan masalah matematis siswa SMA Negeri 2 Mandrehe. Penelitian ini merupakan penelitian kuantitatif dengan metode eksperimen semu (quasi experiment) menggunakan desain Nonequivalent Control Group Design. title: Sistem Rekomendasi Buku Berbasis Content-Based Filtering dengan Menggunakan TF-IDF dan Cosine Similarity
abstractText: Latar Belakang: Meningkatnya jumlah koleksi buku digital menyulitkan pengguna dalam menemukan buku yang sesuai dengan kebutuhannya. Oleh karena itu, diperlukan sistem rekomendasi yang dapat menyajikan buku yang relevan. Tujuan: Penelitian ini bertujuan merancang, mengimplementasikan, dan mengevaluasi sistem rekomendasi buku berbasis Content-Based Filtering (CBF) menggunakan TF-IDF dan Cosine Similarity. Metode: Sistem dibangun menggunakan metode Content-Based Filtering (CBF), dengan TF-IDF dan Cosine Similarity, serta dievaluasi menggunakan metrik Precision, NDCG, dan Running Time pada skenario Top-3, Top-5, dan Top-10. Hasil: Sistem menghasilkan nilai Precision sebesar 0,523 pada Top-3 dan 0,518 pada Top-5, serta 0,508 pada Top-10, serta nilai NDCG sebesar 0,666 pada Top-3 dan 0,688 pada Top-5, serta 0,706 pada Top-10. Nilai Cosine Similarity tertinggi yang diperoleh mencapai 0,550. Kesimpulan: Kombinasi TF-IDF dan Cosine Similarity terbukti efektif dalam menghasilkan rekomendasi buku yang relevan dan terurut dengan baik sesuai tingkat kemiripan konten.

Internal Symmetry-Driven Modal Convergence Enhances Chiral Scattering
abstractText: Abstract Chiral scattering in nanostructures emerges from interference between electric and magnetic modes, yet its associated modal strength, arrangements and spectral concentration cannot be inferred from structural handedness alone. Using plasmonic nanorod dimers as a model system, we combine full-field electromagnetic simulations and single-particle circular differential scattering (CDS) spectroscopy to reveal how rotational and translational reconfigurations reshape modal overlap, coupling, and spectral organization even within an established handed architecture. We show that rotational asymmetry tunes the balance between electric-dipole (ED)- and magnetic-dipole (MD)-dominant chiral modes, while translational asymmetry controls their spectral separation and convergence. Consequently, the center-edge configuration produces enhanced and spectrally concentrated CDS responses coinciding with reduced chiral mode splitting and strengthened ED–MD coupling, a mode convergence regime supported both theoretically and experimentally. These results establish modal convergence as a design criterion for tailoring mode organization and scattering through internal symmetry in chiral nanophotonic systems.

title: Mechanical characteristics of rock fracturing based on tension-shearing breaking process
abstractText: Abstract This work aimed to investigate novel rock fragmentation theories and supporting methodologies for deep hard rock. Rock fragmentation models were established by integrating AutoCAD and Particle Flow Code (PFC) software. Preformed boreholes and rock cutting tools were set in the model, and the cutting tools were pulled along the rock free surface to replicate rock fragmentation evolution. The effects of different D/d ratios, borehole depths, pulling velocities and confining pressures on rock fragmentation characteristics were systematically analyzed. The volume of fractured rock blocks is found to be positively proportional to the D/d ratio. The peak rock-breaking load and microcrack count both increase with D/d ratio and borehole depth. The microcracks exhibit a discrete distribution. The peak rock-breaking load reaches a maximum of 57.72 kN at a D/d ratio of 4. The rock-breaking load peaks at 33.99 kN at a borehole depth of 25 mm. Under confining pressure, microcracks develop in sheet-like distribution, and multiple primary and secondary fracture planes are generated under all working conditions. For pulling velocities of 1, 1.5 and 2 m/s, the minimum peak rock-breaking load is observed at a confining pressure of 10 MPa, namely 28.48, 26.62 and 27.39 kN, respectively. For all tested pulling velocities, the number of microcracks reaches its minimum when the confining pressure ranges from 10 to 15 MPa. Confining pressure exerts both promoting and restraining effects on crack propagation. The research findings can provide theoretical references for the optimization of fragmentation methods applied to deep hard rock masses.
